Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## The goal tape moves `$4C` pixels higher than normal

**Codes:** `1465-6DA0`

**Raw form:** `018273:62`. The original byte is `$75`. SNES Game Genie has no
compare byte, so the code writes the value whatever is there.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:21:22

**Mechanism:** The goal tape is sprite `$7B`. Its entry in the `CallSpriteInit`
table (`$01817D + 2 * $7B` = `$018273`) points at `InitGoalTape` (`$01C075`).
That routine saves the start X and Y (Y goes to `SpriteMisc1528`) and the extra
bits. Just before it, at `$01C062`, is an init wrapper that nothing points to:

```
    JSR InitGoalTape          ; 20 75 C0
    LDA SpriteYPosLow,X / SEC / SBC #$4C / STA SpriteYPosLow,X
    LDA SpriteYPosHigh,X / SBC #$00 / STA SpriteYPosHigh,X
    RTS
```

It runs the normal init, then moves the tape up `$4C` (76) pixels. Both
routines are in page `$01C0`, so the code changes only the low byte of the
table entry, from `$75` to `$62`.

`GoalTape` moves the tape with Y speed `$F0` or `$10` (1 pixel a frame) and
turns it round every `$7C` frames, starting upward. So the tape moves over the
same distance as before, but `$4C` pixels higher.

**Evidence:** `InitGoalTape` is at `$01C075` in `SMW_U.sym`. The ROM holds `75 C0`
at `$018273`. It holds `60 20 75 C0 B5 D8 38 E9 4C 95 D8 BD D4 14 E9 00 9D D4 14
60` from `$01C061`: the `RTS` that ends `CODE_01C05E`, then the unreachable
wrapper at `$01C062`. The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The
effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- `SpriteMisc1528` still holds the original Y, because `InitGoalTape` saves it
  before the wrapper moves the sprite. The test for passing the goal uses
  `SpriteMisc1528`, so walking through the goal ends the level as before.
- Breaking the tape for bonus stars needs Mario to touch the tape sprite. It
  is higher now, so that is harder, and near its top it may be above the
  goal posts or off the top of the screen.
- It changes every goal tape, including secret exits.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`InitGoalTape`) and the
`CallSpriteInit` table base `$01817D`, plus a direct read of `comparison_U.smc`
minus its 512-byte copier header. `tools/linemap_U.tsv` was stale at the time
and was not used.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Ghost house Boo ceilings become the unused Swooper bat ceiling

**Codes:** `3FCA-6F6C`

**Raw form:** `02AAC6:E1`. The original byte is `$E4`. SNES Game Genie has no
compare byte, so the code writes the value whatever is there.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:23:21

**Mechanism:** Level sprites `$E1`-`$E6` start cluster sprites. The level loader
calls `CODE_02AAC0` with the sprite number in A:

```
CODE_02AAC0:
    LDY #$01 / STY ActivateClusterSprite
    CMP #$E4 / BEQ -> JMP CODE_02AA33     ; bat ceiling
    CMP #$E6 / BEQ CODE_02AA6C            ; candle flames
    CMP #$E5 / BEQ CODE_02AA8D            ; reappearing Boos
    CMP #$E2 / BCS CODE_02AB11            ; Boo rings
    ; otherwise ($E1): Boo ceiling, 20 cluster sprites of type $03
```

No level in the game places sprite `$E4`, so `CODE_02AA33` never runs. It fills
cluster slots `$0E` down to `$00` with cluster sprite `$08`, at random X
positions on the screen and at the Y of the level sprite. Type `$08` uses the
same handler as the Boo ceiling (`CODE_02FBC7`). Every 8 frames that handler
wakes one random sprite, and the draw code checks for type `$08` to use
`BatCeilingTiles` (`$AE $AE $C0 $EB`) instead of Boo tiles.

The code changes the first compare from `$E4` to `$E1`. Now the Boo ceiling
sprite takes the bat-ceiling branch. The scan of `lvl/spr` finds sprite `$E1` in
two levels: `004_DGHroom1` and `1FA_FGHroom2`.

**Evidence:** `CODE_02AAC0` is at `$02AAC0` in `SMW_U.sym`. The ROM holds `4C 33 AA`
(the `JMP`) at `$02AABD`, then `A0 01 8C B8 18 C9 E4 F0 F4 C9 E6 F0 9F C9 E5 F0 BC
C9 E2 B0`. The `$E4` is at `$02AAC6`, and `F0 F4` branches back to the `JMP`.
`CODE_02AA33` starts `A2 0E 9E 66 1E 9E 86 0F A9 08 9D 92 18` (`LDX #$0E`, ...,
`LDA #$08 / STA ClusterSpriteNumber,X`). The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The bat tiles come from the level's sprite graphics. A ghost house does not
  load the cave graphics, so the bats may look like other tiles.
- The Boo ceiling sets random Y positions near the top of the screen. The bat
  ceiling puts all 15 bats at the Y where the level placed the sprite, so they
  may form one row, and it may not be at the ceiling.
- There are 15 bats instead of 20 Boos. The handler still picks from 20 slots,
  so some wake-ups do nothing.
- The bat code has more unreachable parts (`bank_02.asm` near
  `BatCeilingTiles`). They have not been traced, so the swoop may behave oddly.
- Sprites `$E2`, `$E3`, `$E5` and `$E6` behave as before. Sprite `$E4`, which no
  level places, would now fall through to the Boo ring branch.
- `BooRingIndex` is not incremented for the bat ceiling.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`CODE_02AAC0`, `CODE_02AA33`) plus a
direct read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. Level list
from a scan of `lvl/spr/*.bin`. `tools/linemap_U.tsv` was stale at the time and
was not used.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## The shaking exploding block gives off rising wisps like a sleeping Rip Van Fish

**Codes:** `DD34-D4DB`

**Raw form:** `02E428:00`. The original byte is `$04`. SNES Game Genie has no
compare byte, so the code writes the value whatever is there.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:31:52

**Mechanism:** The exploding block (sprite `$4C`) shakes until Mario comes near,
then turns into the sprite it holds. Its main routine starts:

```
CODE_02E41F:
    JSL GenericSprGfxRt2      ; 22 B2 90 01
    LDA SpriteLock            ; A5 9D
    BNE Return02E462          ; D0 3B
    BRA +                     ; 80 04
    JSL ADDR_02C0CF           ; 22 CF C0 02   unreachable
  + ...
```

`ADDR_02C0CF` is the unused twin of the Rip Van Fish "Z" spawner `CODE_02C0D9`.
It loads minor extended sprite type `$08` (or `$09` if `SpriteMisc157C` is 1)
instead of `$06`. Then the shared code counts `SpriteMisc1528,X` down, and
each time it passes 0 it resets it to `$28` and spawns the minor sprite at the
sprite's X + 6, timer `$7F`, X speed `$FA`. It does nothing while the sprite is
off-screen.

Minor extended sprites `$06`, `$08` and `$09` all run `CODE_028DDB`. They drift
from side to side and rise 1 pixel every 4 frames. Type `$06` draws the Z tiles
from `RipVanFishZsTiles`. Types `$08` and above draw tile `$7F` instead, and
`$09` drifts the other way.

The code sets the `BRA` displacement to 0, so the `JSL` runs every frame.
`InitExplodingBlk` never sets `SpriteMisc157C`, so the block spawns type `$08`:
one rising tile `$7F` about every 41 frames.

**Evidence:** `CODE_02E41F` is at `$02E41F` in `SMW_U.sym`. The ROM holds `22 B2 90
01 A5 9D D0 3B 80 04 22 CF C0 02 A0 00` there, so the `BRA` operand `$04` is at
`$02E428`. `ADDR_02C0CF` holds `A9 08 BC 7C 15 F0 01 1A 80 02 A9 06`: `LDA #$08`,
`LDY SpriteMisc157C,X`, `BEQ`, `INC A`, `BRA` past `CODE_02C0D9`'s `LDA #$06`.
The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from
the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- What tile `$7F` looks like depends on the sprite graphics the level loads.
  It has not been checked.
- The scan of `lvl/spr` finds the exploding block in `11E_FoI1` (9) and
  `126_SP7` (4).
- The routine is skipped while sprites are locked, as before.
- Each wisp uses one of the 12 minor extended sprite slots for up to `$7F`
  frames. With many blocks on screen they fill up, and then the spawner
  overwrites the oldest one.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`CODE_02E41F`, `ADDR_02C0CF`,
`CODE_028DDB`) plus a direct read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte
copier header. Level list from a scan of `lvl/spr/*.bin`. `tools/linemap_U.tsv`
was stale at the time and was not used.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Mario leaves skid smoke all the time, even in the air, but loses cape spin and fireballs

**Codes:** `0CA6-0F67` + `E3A6-0FA7` + `B2E0-67A7` + `DDE9-64A7`

**Raw form:**
- `00CD86:4A`, original `$62`
- `00CD87:FE`, original `$D0`
- `00FE4F:9D`, original `$72`
- `00FE5B:00`, original `$04`

SNES Game Genie has no compare byte, so the codes write the values whatever is
there. Use all four together.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:34:17

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00FE4A` spawns one skid smoke sprite under Mario's feet. It
is only called while Mario skids, slides while ducking or slides down a slope,
and it has its own checks:

```
CODE_00FE4A:
    LDA TrueFrame / AND #$03   ; only every 4th frame
    ORA PlayerInAir            ; 05 72   not in the air
    ORA PlayerXPosScrRel+1     ; 05 7F   on screen
    ORA PlayerYPosScrRel+1     ; 05 81
    ORA SpriteLock             ; 05 9D   sprites not locked
    BNE Return00FE71
    LDA byetudlrHold / AND #$04 ; 29 04   holding down...
    BEQ CODE_00FE67
    LDA PlayerXSpeed+1 / ... / BCC Return00FE71   ; ...needs some speed
CODE_00FE67: find a free smoke slot, then CODE_00FE72 fills it
```

- Codes 1 and 2 get it called every frame. The normal player update at
  `CODE_00CD82` runs `JSR CODE_00D5F2` (ground/air speed), `JSR CODE_00D062`
  (cape spin and fireballs), `JSR CODE_00D7E4` (cape flight). The codes change
  `JSR CODE_00D062` (`20 62 D0`) to `JSR CODE_00FE4A`. Both routines end in `RTS`,
  and the next call loads its own values, so nothing depends on what they
  leave in A or Y.
- Code 3 changes `ORA PlayerInAir` to a second `ORA SpriteLock`, so smoke also
  spawns in the air. The screen and sprite-lock checks stay.
- Code 4 changes `AND #$04` to `AND #$00`, so the `BEQ` is always taken and
  holding down no longer blocks the smoke.

**Evidence:** `CODE_00CD82` is at `$00CD82` in `SMW_U.sym`. The ROM holds `20 F2 D5 20
62 D0 20 E4 D7 22 B1 CE 00` there. `CODE_00FE4A` holds `A5 13 29 03 05 72 05 7F
05 81 05 9D D0 19 A5 15 29 04 F0 09`. `PlayerInAir` is `$72` and `SpriteLock` is
`$9D`. The codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived
from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **Cape Mario cannot spin with X/Y, and Fire Mario cannot throw fireballs**,
  because `CODE_00D062` no longer runs. Small and big Mario lose nothing.
  Yoshi's fireballs and cape flight are separate and still work.
- There is no smoke while Mario swims, climbs or rides a P-balloon. Those use
  other paths instead of `CODE_00CD82`.
- One smoke spawns every 4 frames and lasts `$13` frames, but there are only 3
  smoke slots. Some puffs are skipped, and smoke from stomps and other
  effects may be missing sometimes.
- The skid, duck-slide and slope-slide calls also lose the air and down-button
  checks, so they can add a second puff on the same frame.
- The smoke is placed for Mario's feet (Y + `$1A`, or `$2A` on Yoshi). In the
  air it rises from below him.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`CODE_00CD82`, `CODE_00FE4A`) and
`rammap.asm`, plus a direct read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier
header. `tools/linemap_U.tsv` was stale at the time and was not used.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## The whole overworld is unlocked: every path is open and every level can be entered

**Codes:** `6D31-DF2F` + `DD21-6FF4` + `6B2C-6DF4` + `6DBC-64FD` + `DDC1-64DD`

**Raw form:**
- `04E467:80`, original `$D0`
- `04DA64:00`, original `$47`
- `04DAA0:89`, original `$77`
- `0492A8:80`, original `$D0`
- `00A268:00`, original `$20`

SNES Game Genie has no compare byte, so the codes write the values whatever is
there. Use all five together.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:40:03

**Mechanism:** When the overworld loads, two loops walk over the 111 overworld
events (`$00`-`$6E`). Each loop reads the event's bit in `OWEventsActivated` and
skips the event if the bit is clear.

- Code 1 is in `CODE_04E453`, the loop that draws each event's tiles (new paths,
  bridges, level dots) into `OWLayer2Tilemap`. It changes `BNE +` / `RTS` to
  `BRA +`, so every event's tiles are drawn.
- Code 2 is in `CODE_04DA49`, the loop that writes each event's change into the
  Map16 walk map at `$7EC800`. It sets the `BEQ Return04DAAC` offset to `$00`,
  so every event's change is applied. Codes 1 and 2 together give the same map
  that the game builds when all the event bits are set.
- Code 3 is also in `CODE_04DA49`. For each event that loop calls
  `JSR CODE_04E677`, which changes a beaten castle or fortress tile to rubble
  (tiles `$81`-`$86`). Only tiles `$56`-`$80` can be entered, so rubble would
  block those levels. The code points the `JSR` at the `RTS` at `$04E689`, so
  the structures stay standing and can be entered.
- Code 4 is in `CODE_04928C`. When you press a direction on a level tile, the
  game ANDs the direction with that level's bits in `OWLevelTileSettings`. On a
  level you have not beaten, only the direction you came from is set. The code
  changes `BNE CODE_0492AD` to `BRA`, so you can leave any level in any
  direction. The walk map check for a path tile still runs after this.
- Code 5 is in `CODE_00A25B`, the Start+Select exit on the pause screen. It
  reads bit `$80` ("beaten") of `OWLevelTileSettings` and returns if it is
  clear. The code sets the `BPL Return00A289` offset to `$00`, so Start+Select
  leaves any level, as if it were beaten.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds:
- `CODE_04E453`: `E2 30 A5 0F 29 07 AA A5 0F 4A 4A 4A A8 B9 02 1F 3F 4B E4 04 D0 01 60`
- `CODE_04DA49`: `C2 30 A5 0F 29 F8 00 4A 4A 4A A8 A5 0F 29 07 00 AA E2 20 B9 02 1F 3F 4B E4 04 F0 47`
- `$04DA9D`: `A5 0F 20 77 E6`
- `CODE_04E677`: `E2 30 A2 17 DF D6 E5 04 F0 09 CA 10 F7 A9 02 8D 86 1B 60` (the `RTS` is at `$04E689`)
- `CODE_04928C`, bytes `$16`-`$20`: `3D A2 1E 29 0F 00 D0 03 4C 11 94`
- `CODE_00A25B`: `A5 15 29 20 F0 28 AC BF 13 B9 A2 1E 10 20`

The codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from
the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The map is built only when the overworld loads. Turn the codes on before you
  load a file, or leave a level to reload the map.
- The codes do not change `OWEventsActivated` or the save data. Saving only
  keeps the levels you really beat, and the exit count does not change.
- All 111 event slots are applied, including any that a normal game never sets.
  This may draw odd tiles in some places.
- When you really beat a level, its event still plays, and it draws a path that
  is already there. A castle or fortress you beat still crumbles, but it
  stands again the next time the map loads.
- A Start+Select exit does not activate an event.
- Other things that check real progress do not change, such as the Special
  World palette and the Koopa graphics.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`CODE_04E453`, `CODE_04DA49`,
`CODE_04E677`, `CODE_04928C`, `CODE_00A25B`) and `rammap.asm`, plus a direct read
of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Boos in Boo rings and Boo ceilings only hurt Mario from their left half

**Codes:** `DDE5-6FD8`

**Raw form:** `02FE74:00`. The original byte is `$02`. SNES Game Genie has no
compare byte, so the code writes the value whatever is there.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:42:57

**Mechanism:** `CODE_02FE71` is the contact check for the Boo ring cluster
sprites and for the Boo ceiling (and the unused bat ceiling). It starts with:

```
LDA #$14
BRA +
LDA #$0C      ; never reached
+ STA _2
```

`_2` is the hit width. Mario is hurt when `PlayerXPosNext - sprite X + $0A` is
below this width, so with `$14` the hit range is from 10 px left of the Boo to
9 px right of it. The code sets the `BRA` offset to `$00`, so the unused
`LDA #$0C` runs. The range is now 10 px left to 1 px right. Mario can overlap
the right part of a Boo and not be hurt. The vertical check does not change.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 14 80 02 A9 0C 85 02 64 03` at `CODE_02FE71`
(`$02FE71`). Its callers are the Boo ring main (`bank_02.asm` near
`BooRingXPosLow`) and the Boo/bat ceiling main (`CODE_02FBC7`). Boo rings
(level sprites `$E2`/`$E3`) are in `013_DSHroom1`, `0ED_DSHroom2`,
`0F8_SGSroom2` and `107_VGHroom1`. Boo ceilings (`$E1`) are in
`004_DGHroom1` and `1FA_FGHroom2`. The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The check runs only every 4th frame for each Boo, as before.
- Other Boos (the big Boo, normal Boos, Boo Buddies) are normal sprites and use
  their own contact check. They do not change.
- The narrow range is not centered, so it looks like the Boo's right half has
  no hitbox. It is not known what the `$0C` width was for.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`CODE_02FE71`) plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The level list is from a
scan of `lvl/spr/*.bin`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## The auto-scroll sprite runs an unused scroll: the screen moves up and down 48 pixels and shakes at each end

**Codes:** `638E-DDB5` + `C386-D495` + `AF86-D4B5`

**Raw form:**
- `05BCF2:8E`, original `$36`
- `05BC89:AE`, original `$4D`
- `05BC8A:C1`, original `$C0`

SNES Game Genie has no compare byte, so the codes write the values whatever is
there. Use all three together. Do not use them with the scroll command 04, 05 or
0A cheats, which patch the same bytes.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:47:28

**Mechanism:** Two unreachable blocks in `bank_05.asm` are the setup and the
per-frame routine of a scroll command that is in neither pointer table.

The setup block starts at `$05BD7B`, right after `CODE_05BD4C`. Its first 19
bytes pick a command from `DATA_05C9E5` (they would put command 01 on Layer 2).
The cheat skips them and starts at the second `REP #$20`, at `$05BD8E`:
- `Layer1ScrollType` = `DATA_05C9E9,bits`. Type 1 means down; any other type
  means up.
- Target Y = `NextLayer1YPos - DATA_05CBC7,bits`, low byte only, stored in
  `Layer1ScrollXPosUpd`.
- Clears the Layer 1 scroll speeds and then falls into `CODE_05BDC9`, which sets
  `Layer1ScrollTimer` to `$FF`.

The per-frame block starts at `$05C1AE`, right after `CODE_05C198`:
- Timer negative (`ADDR_05C1D4`): if `NextLayer1YPos` equals the target, it
  sets the timer to `$30`, stops the scroll, flips bit 0 of `Layer1ScrollType`
  and moves the target by `DATA_05CBC7,bits` (down if the new type is not 0, up
  if it is 0). Then it eases `Layer1ScrollYSpeed` by 1 each frame toward
  `DATA_05CBC8,type` (down for type 1, up for any other) and moves the camera
  (`ADDR_05C31D`).
- Timer `$20` or more: counts down and flips bit 0 of `NextLayer1YPos` each
  frame. This is a 1-pixel shake for 16 frames.
- Timer `$00`-`$1F`: counts down and does not move. When it goes below 0, the
  scroll starts again.

The codes use the auto-scroll sprite `$E8` (command 01), like the command 04
and 0A cheats. Code 1 points its setup entry (`$05BCF2`, normally
`CODE_05BD36`) at `$05BD8E`. Codes 2 and 3 point its per-frame entry
(`$05BC89`, normally `CODE_05C04D`) at `$05C1AE`. The setup does not change
`Layer1ScrollCmd`, so it stays 01.

**Where you see it:** sprite `$E8` is in `009_DP2main`, `00C_BB1main` and
`0C8_yoshiwingsdark` (names from `lvl/spr/`), with `Layer1ScrollBits` 0, 3 and 4.
- `009_DP2main` (bits 0): type 0, distance `$30`. The screen moves up 48 px at up
  to 0.44 px per frame, shakes, waits, moves down 48 px at up to 0.5 px per
  frame, shakes, waits, and repeats. This is the level to try.
- `00C_BB1main` (bits 3) and `0C8_yoshiwingsdark` (bits 4): type 2, and the
  distance comes from the next table (`$10` and `$28`). The screen moves up
  16 or 40 px at 1/16 px per frame and shakes. The type then flips to 3, which
  also moves up, so the screen never gets back to its target. It keeps moving up
  until the camera stops.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds:
- `$05BD7B`: `AD 40 14 0A A8 C2 20 B9 E5 C9 8D 3E 14 B9 E7 C9 8D 40 14 C2 20 AC 40 14 AD 56 14 ...`
- `$05C1AE`: `AD 56 14 4A 4A AA BD 44 14 30 1B DE 44 14 BD 44 14 C9 20 90 0E C2 20 AE 56 14 BD 64 14 49 01 00 9D 64 14 4C 2B C3`, followed by `ADDR_05C1D4` (`C2 30`) at `$05C1D4`
- setup table entry 01 at `$05BCF2`: `36 BD`; per-frame table entry 01 at `$05BC89`: `4D C0`
- `DATA_05C9E9` starts `00 00 02 02 02`, `DATA_05CBC7` is `30`, and `DATA_05CBC8` starts `70 80 10 28`

`ADDR_05C1D4`, `ADDR_05C31D` and `CODE_05BDC9` are in `SMW_U.sym`. The codes
round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Enter the level with the codes already on. The setup runs once, when the
  sprite spawns.
- The level loses its normal auto-scroll. The normal auto-scroll setup clears
  `HorizLayer1Setting`, and this one does not, so the screen follows Mario
  sideways as in a normal level.
- The target is an exact Y position. If the normal vertical camera moves the
  screen (for example when Mario flies or climbs), the screen may miss the
  target and keep moving until the camera stops.
- The target keeps only the low byte, so a camera Y below `$30` or above `$FF`
  gives a wrong target.
- Moving the screen away from Mario may put him off the bottom of the screen.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and `rammap.asm`, plus a direct read
of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The level list is from
the scan done for the command 04, 05 and 0A cheats.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Yoshi's House is replaced by the beta boss test level (or another beta level in bank 06)

**Codes:** `763D-A7F0` + `6F3D-A790` + `D13D-A7B0` + `123D-64F5`

(orig `$07`) + `05EE08:6D` (orig `$59`)

Entering Yoshi's House loads the unused beta boss test level
(`BossTestBetaLevel`, `$068138`): 11 screens, castle music, a 300 timer. The
first three codes point Yoshi's House's Layer 1 data at the level. `123D-64F5`
removes Yoshi's House's sprites.

cheats. Use only one at a time, because they patch the same bytes. Each one also
uses `123D-64F5`.

| Level | Codes | Raw form (original) |

| **Beta clouds** (`CloudsBetaLevel`, `$068063`) | `173D-A7F0` + `D13D-A7B0` + `123D-64F5` | `05E30C:63` (`$2D`) + `05E30E:06` (`$07`) + `05EE08:6D` (`$59`) |

| **Beta Wendy room** (`WendyBetaLevel`, `$0683AB`, Layer 2 `$068501`) | `C83D-A7F0` + `673D-A790` + `D13D-A7B0` + `DF3D-07F1` + `693D-0791` + `D13D-07B1` + `123D-64F5` | `05E30C:AB` + `05E30D:83` + `05E30E:06` + `05E90C:01` + `05E90D:85` + `05E90E:06` + `05EE08:6D` |

| **First unused ghost house exit** (`UnusedGHExitLevel`, `$068675`, Layer 2 `$06861B`) | `593D-A7F0` + `613D-A790` + `D13D-A7B0` + `F83D-07F1` + `613D-0791` + `D13D-07B1` + `123D-64F5` | `05E30C:75` + `05E30D:86` + `05E30E:06` + `05E90C:1B` + `05E90D:86` + `05E90E:06` + `05EE08:6D` |

SNES Game Genie has no compare byte, so the codes write the values whatever is
there. The original bytes are `$05E30C` = `2D 80 07`, `$05E90C` = `00 D9 FF` and
`$05EE08` = `59 E7`.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 22:50:38

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `curated`

**Mechanism:** The level loader in `bank_05.asm` reads three pointers for the
level number:
- `Layer1Ptrs` (`$05E000`, 3 bytes per level): the Layer 1 data. The first 5
  bytes of that data are the level header.
- `Layer2Ptrs` (`$05E600`, 3 bytes per level): Layer 2 data, or a background
  image when the third byte is `$FF`.
- `Ptrs05EC00` (2 bytes per level, bank `$07` always): the sprite list.

Yoshi's House is level `$104`. Its Layer 1 pointer is at `$05E30C` (`$07802D`),
its Layer 2 pointer at `$05E90C` (a background image), and its sprite pointer at
`$05EE08` (`$07E759`).

- The Layer 1 codes point Yoshi's House at a level in bank `$06`. None of these
  eight levels is named by any pointer table.
- The beta lava cave, the beta Wendy room and the unused ghost house exit have
  Layer 2 level data of their own (level mode `$01` or `$02`). For them, the
  Layer 2 codes point at that data. For the ghost house
  exit this is `GhostHouseExitLvlL2`, the Layer 2 data that the real ghost house
  exit uses.
- `123D-64F5` changes the sprite pointer from `$E759` to `$E76D`, a sprite list
  with no sprites (`00 FF`). Without it, the Yoshi's House sprites (message
  boxes, birds, Yoshi, smoke) spawn in the new level, drawn with the wrong
  sprite tiles.

The level header decides the size, music, timer and tilesets:

| Level | Header | Screens | Mode | Object tileset | Sprite tileset | Music | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Beta boss test | `6A 60 31 8B 21` | 11 | `$00` | 1 | 1 | castle | 300 |
| Beta clouds | `07 00 02 80 30` | 8 | `$00` | 0 | 2 | overworld | 300 |
| Beta mushrooms | `27 20 22 51 02` | 8 | `$00` | 2 | 2 | athletic | 200 |
| Beta lava cave | `CA 62 13 A2 03` | 11 | `$02` | 3 | 3 | underground | 300 |
| Beta twin blocks | `61 60 31 CB 11` | 2 | `$00` | 1 | 1 | castle | 400 |
| Beta Wendy room | `6B 62 31 8B 01` | 12 | `$02` | 1 | 1 | castle | 300 |
| Beta "just ground" | `67 40 54 1C 15` | 8 | `$00` | 5 | 4 | underwater | none |
| First unused ghost house exit | `C1 A1 49 84 05` | 2 | `$01` | 5 | 9 | ghost house | 300 |

Screens = (byte 0 AND `$1F`) + 1; mode = byte 1 AND `$1F`; sprite tileset =
byte 2 AND `$0F`; music = `LevelMusicTable` entry (byte 2 >> 4) AND 7; timer =
`TimerTable` entry byte 3 >> 6 (`00 02 03 04`, in hundreds); object tileset =
byte 4 AND `$0F`.

The first unused ghost house exit starts with the same header and first object
as the real one (`GhostHouseExitLevel`, `$068621`). The rest of its object data
is different.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `2D 80 07` at `$05E30C`, `00 D9 FF` at `$05E90C`,
`59 E7` at `$05EE08`, and `00 FF` at `$07E76D`. The headers above are the first
5 bytes at each label address in `SMW_U.sym`. `$07E76D` is named by another
entry in `Ptrs05EC00`, so it is a real empty sprite list. The codes round-trip
through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effects are derived from the disassembly and
**have not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **The ending uses this level slot too.** `GM1DLoadThankYou` loads Yoshi's
  House for the "Thank You" scene, so that scene gets the beta level as well.
- Mario's start position still comes from Yoshi's House's entry in
  `DATA_05F200`/`DATA_05FE00`. He starts on the first screen at Yoshi's House's
  position, and there may be no floor under him.
- The five levels without their own Layer 2 data keep Yoshi's House's background
  image, which was not drawn for them.
- Other level settings indexed by level number (`DATA_05F000` and the tables
  after it) are still Yoshi's House's.
- These are unfinished levels. Expect missing objects, no goal, and parts that
  look wrong. If there is no way out, die or reset.
- Turn the codes off before you use a different beta level cheat. Do not use
  them with the other Yoshi's House replacement cheats.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` (`Layer1Ptrs`, `Layer2Ptrs`, the
level labels) plus a direct read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier
header. The empty sprite list was found by scanning all 512 `Ptrs05EC00`
entries.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Yoshi's House is replaced by the title screen demo level, and you can play it

**Codes:** `893D-A7F0` + `693D-A790` + `D13D-A7B0` + `9B3D-07F1` + `2E3D-0791` + `453D-64F5` + `A03D-6495` + `9CED-0FF0` + `DDED-AFF0`

**Raw form:**
- `05E30C:B5`, original `$2D`
- `05E30D:85`, original `$80`
- `05E30E:06`, original `$07`
- `05E90C:59`, original `$00`
- `05E90D:DF`, original `$D9`
- `05EE08:27`, original `$59`
- `05EE09:C4`, original `$E7`
- `05F104:5A`, original `$0B`
- `05F304:00`, original `$01`

SNES Game Genie has no compare byte, so the codes write the values whatever is
there. Use all nine together.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 23:22:12

**Mechanism:** The title screen demo is level `$0C7` (`!TitleScreenLevel`).
`GM03LoadTitleScreen` loads it through `OverworldOverride`, and the demo plays
it with recorded inputs. You cannot normally play it.

Yoshi's House is level `$104`. The level loader in `bank_05.asm` reads these
per-level entries, and the codes copy level `$0C7`'s entries into level `$104`'s:

| Table | Level `$0C7` | Level `$104` | Codes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Layer1Ptrs` (`$05E000`, 3 bytes) | `B5 85 06` (`TitleScrLevel0C7`) | `2D 80 07` | 1-3 |
| `Layer2Ptrs` (`$05E600`, 3 bytes) | `59 DF FF` (background) | `00 D9 FF` | 4-5 |
| `Ptrs05EC00` (2 bytes, bank `$07`) | `27 C4` (`TitleScrSprites0C7`) | `59 E7` | 6-7 |
| `DATA_05F000` | `$5A` | `$0B` | 8 |
| `DATA_05F200` | `$00` | `$01` | 9 |
| `DATA_05F400`, `DATA_05F600` | `$0A`, `$00` | same | none |
| `DATA_05F800`-`DATA_05FE00` | `$00` | same | none |

- `DATA_05F000` holds the Layer 2 scroll setting (high 4 bits) and Mario's
  start Y (low 4 bits).
- `DATA_05F200` holds the Layer 3 setting (bits 6-7), the entrance type (bits
  3-5) and Mario's start X (bits 0-2).

After the codes, the only difference is the level number. The title screen code
that depends on `OverworldOverride` does not run, so the level plays as a normal
level.

Header of `TitleScrLevel0C7`: `47 C0 85 00 00`. That is 8 screens, level mode
`$00`, object tileset 0, sprite tileset 5, the overworld music and no time
limit. Its sprite list (`$07C427`) has sprites `$05`, `$BD`, `$04`, `$05`, `$06`,
`$07`, `$70` and `$4F`.

**Evidence:** The ROM bytes in the table above were read at `$05E000 + 3 ×
level`, `$05E600 + 3 × level`, `$05EC00 + 2 × level` and `$05F000`-`$05FE00 +
level`. `TitleScrLevel0C7` is at `$0685B5` in `SMW_U.sym`, and `bank_05.asm`
names it at `dl TitleScrLevel0C7` and `dw TitleScrSprites0C7`. The codes
round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **The ending uses this level slot too.** `GM1DLoadThankYou` loads Yoshi's
  House for the "Thank You" scene, so that scene gets the demo level as well.
- The demo level was built for a short recorded run. It may have no goal or
  exit. If there is no way out, die or reset.
- The music is the level's own overworld track, not the title screen music.
- Do not use these codes with the other Yoshi's House replacement cheats.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and `constants.asm`, plus a direct
read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Short overworld unlock: every path is shown and you can leave any level in any direction (3 codes)

**Codes:** `6D31-DF2F` + `6DBC-64FD` + `DDC1-64DD`

**Raw form:**
- `04E467:80`, original `$D0`
- `0492A8:80`, original `$D0`
- `00A268:00`, original `$20`

SNES Game Genie has no compare byte, so the codes write the values whatever is
there. The first two codes are enough to reach the levels. The third one is
optional.

**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 23:34:01

**Mechanism:** This is the 5-code overworld unlock without its codes 2 and 3.
Those two only change how some tiles look, so they are not needed to reach the
levels.

- Where Mario can walk comes from the Layer 1 overworld tile map at `$7EC800`.
  `DecompressOverworldL2` copies it whole from `OWL1TileData`, then
  `CODE_04D7F2` numbers every tile in the level range `$56`-`$80`. Events do not
  add path tiles to this map. Every path tile (`$01`-`$55`) and level tile is
  there from the start, before any event runs.
- **What stops you** is `OWLevelTileSettings`. When you press a direction on a
  level tile, `CODE_04928C` ANDs it with that level's direction bits (`$01`-`$08`).
  On a level you have not beaten, only the direction you came from is set.
- Code 2 (`0492A8:80`) changes the `BNE CODE_0492AD` there to `BRA`, so you can
  leave any level in any direction that has a path.
- Code 1 (`04E467:80`) makes `CODE_04E453` draw every event's tiles when the map
  loads, so the paths you can now walk on are visible.
- Code 3 (`00A268:00`) lets Start+Select on the pause screen leave any level.
  Without it, you must finish or die to leave a level you have not beaten.

The other loop, `CODE_04DA49`, runs after `CODE_04D7F2` has numbered the level
tiles. It only swaps tiles for other tiles (for example a hidden level tile
`$6E`-`$75` for its visible form `$66`-`$6D`, or a fortress `$76` for `$77`), and
turns beaten castles into rubble. The swaps do not change where Mario can walk
(`$01`-`$86`) or which tiles count as levels. So leaving it out keeps every
level reachable, and the castles stay standing.

**About "treat every level as beaten":** the "beaten" flag is bit `$80` of
`OWLevelTileSettings`. The Start+Select exit reads it, and so does a music check
that only some releases have. Setting it would not open any paths.
Movement uses the direction bits, and code 2 is what treats every level as open.

**Evidence:** Same bytes as the 5-code unlock section: `CODE_04E453` has `D0 01
60` at `$04E467`, `CODE_04928C` has `D0 03 4C 11 94` at `$0492A8`, and
`CODE_00A25B` has `10 20` at `$00A267`. `DecompressOverworldL2`'s `MVN` from
`OWL1TileData` to `Map16TilesLow`, followed by `JSR CODE_04D7F2`, is at
`bank_04.asm` just before `CODE_04DC6A`. The codes round-trip through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Turn the codes on before you load a file, or leave a level to reload the map.
- Hidden level tiles keep their hidden form, and levels you have not beaten keep
  their normal colour. They can still be entered.
- Some path tiles keep their old look, because the tile swap does not run.
- The save data does not change.
- Beating a level still plays its event as normal.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every sliding shell-less Koopa is the unused winged cage instead

**Codes:** `5C60-AF69` + `6660-AFA9`
**Raw form:** `018746:7A` (orig `$8E`) + `018747:88` (orig `$87`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-13 23:42:00

**Mechanism:** Sprite `$BD` is the shell-less blue Koopa that slides down a slope
and is already moving when it appears. It is the Koopa at the start of Yoshi's
Island 1. Its per-frame entry in the `CallSpriteMain` table (`$0185CC`) is
`Bank3SprHandler` (`$01878E`). The two codes change that entry, both bytes, to
`WingedCage` (`$01887A`). See "Every Wiggler is the unused winged cage instead"
for what the cage code does: 4 pairs of flapping wings, Layer 3 scrolled to
follow it, and an invisible `$90`-pixel box that holds Mario.

Only entry `$BD` changes. `Bank3SprHandler` is also used by many other sprites,
through their own entries, and they are not affected.

The setup routine is left as it is. `InitSlidingKoopa` only stores `$04` in
`SpriteMisc1540,X` (a timer). `WingedCageMain` and its wing-drawing routine
`ADDR_02CCB9` never read `SpriteMisc1540`, so the timer does
nothing. The cage's own setup routine does nothing at all.

**Where you see it:** Sprite `$BD` is placed once in `105_YI1main` (the first
sprite in the level), 4 times in `010_CMmain`, once in `128_SP5`, and once in
`0C7_titlescreen` (names from `lvl/spr/`).

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `8E 87` at `$018746` (`$0185CC + 2 × $BD`), which
the source lists as `dw Bank3SprHandler ; BD - Sliding Koopa without a shell`.
It holds `8B A9 02 48 AB 22 FE CB 02 AB 60` at `$01887A` (`WingedCage`). The
init entry at `$0182F7` holds `7D 83` (`InitSlidingKoopa`, `LDA #$04` then
`STA SpriteMisc1540,X / RTS`). Level sprite data was scanned with the
1-header-byte, 3-bytes-per-sprite, `$FF`-terminated format. Both codes
round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Use both codes together. With only one, the entry points into the middle of
  other code and the game will likely crash when a sliding Koopa appears.
- The same caveats as the Wiggler cheat apply: Mario may be dragged to the
  cage's X, the floor rule pulls him up, and the 16 wing tiles can take OAM
  from other sprites.
- The sprite keeps sprite `$BD`'s properties (how it reacts to stomps, fireballs
  and so on), because those come from other tables.
- The title screen demo also has one. Its recorded inputs may not work with the
  cage there, so the demo may play out differently.
- The wing tiles come from the sprite graphics the level loads. They may not
  look like wings.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and the `CallSpriteMain` table in
`bank_01.asm`, plus a direct read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte
copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Mario can pick up and carry almost any enemy

**Code:** `DDCB-DD01`
**Raw form:** `01A891:00` (orig `$05`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 20:57:09

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `video-ready` `curated`

**Mechanism:** Most sprites check contact with Mario through
`MarioSprInteractRt`. After a hit is found, and after the star check, the code
at `CODE_01A87E` reads the sprite's status. If the status is 9 (stunned, like a
shell that is not moving), it calls `CODE_01AA42`, the routine that lets Mario
pick the sprite up or kick it. Any other status goes on to the normal code,
where Mario stomps the sprite or gets hurt. The status test is
`LDA SpriteStatus,X / CMP #$09 / BNE +`. The code sets the `BNE` displacement
to `$00`, so both outcomes of the branch fall through to `JSR CODE_01AA42`.
Every sprite that uses this path is now treated like a stunned shell.

So, when Mario touches one of these sprites:
- **Y or X held** (and Mario is not already carrying something or riding
  Yoshi): `CODE_01AA42` sets the status to `$0B` (carried). Mario holds the
  sprite like a shell. Let go of the button to kick it, or hold Down to set it
  down.
- **No button held:** Mario kicks the sprite, like a shell.
- **Spin jump or riding Yoshi, from above:** the sprite is spin-killed as
  normal, if it can be jumped on.

108 sprites use this path. Some of them: all the Koopas and Goombas, Bob-omb,
Buzzy Beetle, Spiny, Bullet Bill, Banzai Bill, Torpedo Ted, Lakitu,
Magikoopa, Thwomp, Thwimp, Big Boo, Boo, the Piranha Plants, Monty Moles,
Pokey, Super Koopas, Dino Rhino and Dino Torch, Hammer and Sumo Brothers,
Blargg, Bowser's bowling ball, MechaKoopa, the line-guided chainsaws, Grinders
and Fuzzies, and the Key and POW (which Mario can already carry).

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `BD C8 14 C9 09 D0 05 20 42 AA` at `$01A88B`
(`LDA SpriteStatus,X / CMP #$09 / BNE +5 / JSR CODE_01AA42`). The branch
target is `$01A897`, past `CODE_01A895`'s `CLC / RTS`. `CODE_01AA42` is the
routine the status-9 path already uses. It reads `byetudlrHold` bit 6 and
`CarryingFlag`, then writes status `$0B` and `PickUpItemTimer`. The list of
affected sprites comes from bit 7 of each entry in `Sprite167AVals`
(`SpriteTweakerD`). `MarioSprInteractRt` returns early for sprites with that
bit set. The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is
derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **Enemies that use this path can no longer hurt Mario by touch.** Touching
  one kicks it. This includes shells that are already moving. Their fireballs,
  hammers and other projectiles that use their own contact code still hurt.
- Sprites with their own Mario contact code are not affected. These include
  the Chargin' Chuck family, Rex, Dry Bones, Bony Beetle, Wiggler, the Koopa
  Kids, Reznor, the Mega Mole, the fish, Yoshi, the power-ups and the
  platforms.
- A sprite is drawn by the shell code while it is carried, stunned or kicked
  (`CODE_01A187` → `CODE_019806`, frame 6 of `GenericSprGfxRt2`). Many sprites
  will look wrong. Sprites `$54` and higher (Banzai Bill, Hammer Brother,
  chainsaws and so on) read past the end of `SprTilemapOffset`, so they show a
  wrong tile. Big sprites are drawn as one 16x16 tile.
- After Mario sets a sprite down, it stays in status 9 like a shell. The grab
  does not set the stun timer, so if and when it goes back to normal has not
  been traced.
- With a star, the star check comes first and kills most of these sprites on
  touch, so Mario cannot pick them up.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and instruction sizes, plus a direct
read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The linemap was
stale this session.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every sprite is a goal-tape power-up (status C)

**Code:** `DA65-0DA0`
**Raw form:** `018173:0C` (orig `$08`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 21:05:42

**Mechanism:** A new sprite starts in status 1. On its first frame
`HandleSprite` sends it to `CallSpriteInit`, which does
`LDA #$08 / STA SpriteStatus,X` (status 8, normal) and then runs the sprite's
own init. The code changes the `#$08` to `#$0C`. Status C is the status the
game gives the power-up that comes out of an item carried past the goal tape
(`LvlEndPowerUp` in bank 0 writes it directly). So every sprite that goes
through init is set to status C and stays there until something else changes
its status.

Each frame, `HandleSprite` dispatches status C to `HandleGoalPowerup`:
`JSR CallSpriteMain` (the sprite's normal main routine), then
`SubOffscreen0Bnk1`, then `SubUpdateSprPos` again, then two `DEC SpriteYSpeed`
and a ground check. So:
- **Sprites that do not check their status** (Koopas, Goombas, Buzzy Beetles,
  Spinies and the other `Spr0to13Main` sprites) run their normal code and then
  move a second time. They move at about **double speed**, and they fall a
  little slower, because the two `DEC`s take 2 off the 3 that
  `SubUpdateSprPos` adds each time.
- **Sprites whose main routine tests `SpriteStatus == 8`** take their
  "not normal" path instead. These include Thwomp, Thwimp, the Chargin' Chuck
  family, Rex, Dino Rhino and Dino Torch, MechaKoopa, Boo and the Boo Block,
  Eerie, the Sumo Brother, Grinder, Mega Mole, Pokey, the sliding Koopa, the
  Porcu-Puffer and Yoshi. Many of them will only be drawn and fall, or act
  oddly.
- **Sprites stop touching each other.** `SubSprSprInteract` handles only
  statuses 8 to B, and returns at once for status C. Enemies walk through
  each other, and shells do not kill status-C enemies.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 08 9D C8 14` at `$018172` (`CallSpriteInit`:
`LDA #$08 / STA SpriteStatus,X`). `HandleSprite` at `$018127` holds
`BD C8 14 F0 25 C9 08 D0 03 4C C3 85 22 DF 86 00`, and entry C of its
`ExecutePtr` table is `HandleGoalPowerup`. The list of sprites that test for
status 8 comes from a scan of banks 1-3 for
`LDA SpriteStatus,X / CMP #$08 / BNE|BEQ`, grouped by the nearest named label.
The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from
the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- "Always" is only true until something writes a new status. A stomp, a spin
  jump, a star, a kick or a pick-up still changes the status in the normal way.
  Code that writes status 8 directly, without going through init (for example
  a stunned sprite that wakes up), gives status 8 back.
- Mario's contact with a status-C sprite is the normal stomp-or-hurt code,
  because the pick-up path wants status 9.
- Yoshi checks for status 8. With status C, `Yoshi` clears
  `CarryYoshiThruLvls` and jumps to `HandleOffYoshi`, so a Yoshi placed in a
  level will not work normally.
- The sprite scan found the tests, but not what each sprite does on its
  "not normal" path. Some sprites may do more than draw.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The linemap was stale
this session.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every sprite dies the moment it appears (status 2)

**Code:** `D465-0DA0`
**Raw form:** `018173:02` (orig `$08`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 21:07:48

**Mechanism:** A sprite placed in a level is loaded with status 1. On its
first frame `HandleSprite` sends it to `CallSpriteInit`, which does
`LDA #$08 / STA SpriteStatus,X` (status 8, normal) and then runs the sprite's
own init. The code changes the `#$08` to `#$02`, the status for a sprite that
has been killed and falls off the screen. From the next frame,
`HandleSprKilled` runs the sprite: it falls with gravity, drawn upside down
(`HandleSpriteDeath`), until `SubOffscreen0Bnk1` erases it below the screen.
It gives no points and cannot hurt Mario.

Some sprites take a different death path, the same one they take when killed
in the normal game:
- Sprites with the "disappears in a puff of smoke" flag (bit 7 of
  `SpriteTweakerA`) turn into a puff of smoke (status 4).
- Wiggler, and sprites whose main routine handles their own death (bit 0 of
  `SpriteTweakerD`, for example Yoshi), run their main routine instead.
- A throw block breaks. A Lakitu resets `LakituCloudTimer`.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 08 9D C8 14` at `$018172` (`CallSpriteInit`:
`LDA #$08 / STA SpriteStatus,X`). Entry 2 of `HandleSprite`'s `ExecutePtr`
table is `HandleSprKilled`. `ZeroSpriteTables` clears the speeds before init,
so a sprite starts to fall from rest. The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **Most levels cannot be finished normally.** The goal tape (`$7B`) is a
  placed sprite, has no puff-of-smoke flag, and falls away like the rest.
  Keys, P-switches, springboards, platforms and bosses fall away too. Exits
  through pipes and doors still work if Mario can reach them.
- Sprites that are made without going through `CallSpriteInit` keep status 8
  and act normally. That includes the Bullet Bill, Super Koopa, Eerie, fish
  and Para-enemy generators, Torpedo Ted, Magikoopa's magic, the item box
  drop and the Silver P-switch coins.
- A sprite erased by `SubOffscreen0Bnk1` may load again when its spot scrolls
  back into view, and then fall again.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. Tweaker bits from
`Sprite1656Vals` and `Sprite167AVals` in `bank_07.asm`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every sprite is squashed flat the moment it appears (status 3)

**Code:** `D765-0DA0`
**Raw form:** `018173:03` (orig `$08`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 21:07:49

**Mechanism:** A sprite placed in a level is loaded with status 1. On its
first frame `CallSpriteInit` does `LDA #$08 / STA SpriteStatus,X` (status 8,
normal) and then runs the sprite's own init. The code changes the `#$08` to
`#$03`, the status of a sprite Mario has stomped flat. `HandleSprSmushed`
shows the flat sprite until `SpriteMisc1540,X` reaches 0, then clears the
status. A stomp sets that timer to `$20`, but here nothing does:
`ZeroSpriteTables` clears it before init, and most inits do not set it. So on
the next frame `HandleSprSmushed` finds the timer at 0 and clears the status
at once, before it draws anything. On the frame after that, `HandleSprite`
sees status 0 and runs `EraseSprite`, which sets `SpriteLoadIndex` to `$FF` so
the sprite does not load again.

The result: **almost every placed sprite vanishes as it scrolls into view.** A
sprite whose init sets `SpriteMisc1540` (for example the sliding Koopa, which
sets 4) lies flat for that many frames first.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 08 9D C8 14` at `$018172` (`CallSpriteInit`).
Entry 3 of `HandleSprite`'s `ExecutePtr` table is `HandleSprSmushed`, which
starts `LDA SpriteLock / BNE / LDA SpriteMisc1540,X / BNE + / STZ
SpriteStatus,X / RTS`. `ZeroSpriteTables` does `STZ SpriteMisc1540,X`. The
code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **Most levels cannot be finished normally.** The goal tape, keys,
  P-switches, springboards, platforms and bosses vanish too.
- Sprites made without going through `CallSpriteInit` keep status 8 and act
  normally: the Bullet Bill, Super Koopa, Eerie, fish and Para-enemy
  generators, Torpedo Ted, Magikoopa's magic, the item box drop and the Silver
  P-switch coins.
- The status-2 code (`D465-0DA0`) is similar, but there the sprites can be
  seen falling away.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every enemy turns into a shell Mario can carry and throw (status A)

**Code:** `DC65-0DA0`
**Raw form:** `018173:0A` (orig `$08`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 21:07:50

**Mechanism:** A sprite placed in a level is loaded with status 1. On its
first frame `CallSpriteInit` does `LDA #$08 / STA SpriteStatus,X` (status 8,
normal) and then runs the sprite's own init. The code changes the `#$08` to
`#$0A`, the status of a kicked shell. But `HandleSprKicked` first checks the
sprite's X speed. If `SpriteMisc1528,X` is 0 and the speed is less than `$20`
either way, it calls `CODE_01AA0B`, which sets status 9 (stunned). A new
sprite has X speed 0 (`ZeroSpriteTables` clears it, and `InitStandardSprite`
only picks a facing), so **almost every sprite is stunned on its first frame**.

A stunned sprite acts like a shell that is not moving:
- It does not move or attack, and it does not hurt Mario.
- Mario can pick it up with Y or X, carry it, and throw or kick it.
- A kicked one really is kicked (status A, with shell speed from
  `ShellSpeedX`), and kills other sprites it hits.

It is drawn by the stunned-shell graphics code (`CODE_01A187`). Sprites with
their own stunned graphics (Goomba, Bob-omb, MechaKoopa, key, P-switch,
springboard, throw block, baby Yoshi) use those. The others use frame 6 of
`GenericSprGfxRt2` through `CODE_019806`, so many look wrong. Sprites `$54`
and higher read past `SprTilemapOffset` and show a wrong tile.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 08 9D C8 14` at `$018172` (`CallSpriteInit`).
Entry A of `HandleSprite`'s `ExecutePtr` table is `HandleSprKicked`, which
checks `SpriteMisc187B`, then bit 4 of `SpriteTweakerD` (which goes to
`CODE_01AA0B` at once), then `SpriteMisc1528` and `SpriteXSpeed + $20 < $40`
(`CODE_01AA0B` again). `CODE_01AA0B` writes status 9. `ZeroSpriteTables`
clears `SpriteXSpeed`, `SpriteMisc1528`, `SpriteMisc187B` and `SpriteTableC2`.
The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from
the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- A sprite whose init sets an X speed of `$20` or more either way stays
  kicked. It slides like a shell at that speed and kills other sprites. Which
  inits do this has not been checked one by one.
- **The goal tape is stunned too**, so its main routine never runs and it
  cannot end the level. Platforms, springboards, Yoshi and bosses are stunned
  in the same way. Keys and P-switches still work, because stunned is their
  normal state.
- A stunned sprite does not wake up. `CODE_01AA0B` sets no stun timer when
  `SpriteTableC2` is 0.
- Sprites made without going through `CallSpriteInit` keep status 8 and act
  normally: the Bullet Bill, Super Koopa, Eerie, fish and Para-enemy
  generators, Torpedo Ted, Magikoopa's magic, the item box drop and the Silver
  P-switch coins.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Beaten enemies can come back, and some enemies load twice (EraseSprite disabled)

**Code:** `1D69-0D00`
**Raw form:** `018151:60` (orig `$A9`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 21:09:21

**Mechanism:** Each sprite slot has a `SpriteLoadIndex`: the number of the
level sprite that was loaded into it. When a sprite goes off the screen,
`OffScrEraseSprite` uses that number to clear the level sprite's entry in
`SpriteLoadStatus`, so it can load again when its place scrolls back into
view. A slot holding a sprite that was not loaded from the level should have
`$FF` there, which means "do not reload anything".

Most sprites made at run time do not set `SpriteLoadIndex` (`ZeroSpriteTables`
does not clear it). This includes a Koopa knocked out of its shell, power-ups
from blocks, and a sprite spawned from another sprite. They depend on
`EraseSprite`. Every frame, `HandleSprite` runs `EraseSprite` for each empty
slot (status 0), and it does `LDA #$FF / STA SpriteLoadIndex,X / RTS`. The
code changes the `LDA` opcode to `RTS`, so an empty slot keeps the number of
the level sprite it last held.

Then when a run-time sprite in that slot goes off the screen (with status 8
or higher), `OffScrEraseSprite` clears the load flag of that old level sprite:
- If the old sprite was beaten, it **comes back** the next time its place
  scrolls into view.
- If the old sprite had scrolled away and loaded again into a different slot,
  the level loader can **load a second copy** while the first one is still
  there.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 FF 9D 1A 16 60` at `$018151` (`EraseSprite`:
`LDA #$FF / STA SpriteLoadIndex,X / RTS`). `HandleSprite` is its only caller
(`BEQ EraseSprite` for status 0, and entry 0 of the `ExecutePtr` table).
`OffScrEraseSprite` skips the reload only when the status is under 8 or
`SpriteLoadIndex` is `$FF`. The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`.
The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in
play**.

**Caveats:**
- Nothing looks different until a run-time sprite leaves the screen, so the
  effect is easy to miss. It shows best where many sprites spawn and scroll
  away, for example stomping Koopas and then going back.
- A sprite that is killed (status under 8) and then scrolls off still does not
  reload. The change is only in slots that are reused.
- Some spawners set `SpriteLoadIndex` to `$FF` themselves (for example the
  generators), so the sprites they make are not affected.
- The level loader writes the right number for every sprite it loads, so
  level sprites are not affected in their own slots.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Flying ? blocks always give a 1-Up

**Codes:** `CBC9-0405` + `7DC9-0465` (both are needed)
**Raw form:** `01AD59:A9` (orig `$B5`) + `01AD5A:30` (orig `$E4`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 21:44:54

**Mechanism:** The flying `?` blocks are sprites `$83` (flies left) and `$84`
(flies back and forth). `InitFlying_Block` picks the block's item from its X
position: `LDA SpriteXPosLow,X / LSR ×4 / AND #$03 / STA SpriteMisc151C,X`.
When Mario hits the block from below, `Flying_Block` loads that number into Y,
adds 4 if Mario is small, and reads `DATA_01AE88,Y`:

| `151C` | Big Mario | Small Mario |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| 0      | coin      | 1-Up        |
| 1      | flower    | mushroom    |
| 2      | feather   | mushroom    |
| 3      | 1-Up      | 1-Up        |

The value goes to `CODE_02887D`, the routine that makes an item come out of a
block. The codes change `LDA SpriteXPosLow,X` (`B5 E4`) to `LDA #$30`
(`A9 30`). `$30` shifted right four times is 3, so every flying block gets
item number 3, and both table entries for 3 are `$05`, the 1-Up.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `B5 E4 4A 4A 4A 4A 29 03 9D 1C 15` at `$01AD59`,
and `DATA_01AE88` at `$01AE88` holds `06 02 04 05 06 01 01 05`. In
`CODE_02887D`, value 5 selects sprite `$78` (1-Up) and value 6 is the coin.
The codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from
the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Use both codes. With only the first one, the block loads `#$E4` and gets
  item 2 (feather, or mushroom for small Mario).
- The flying blocks are found in only a few levels. By sprite file:
  `$83` in `009_DP2main`, `022_CI1main1`, `105_YI1main`, `10A_VD3main`,
  `11A_VD1main`, `1FA_FGHroom2` and `1FC_C1room2`; `$84` in `125_SP8` and
  `1CA_YI2sub`.
- `Flying_Block` gives an item on each hit until `SpriteTableC2` reaches 2, so
  a block can give up to two 1-Ups. This is also true without the code.
- Unused sprite `$85` shares `InitFlying_Block`, so it is changed too.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Sprite slot 0 takes every sprite-to-sprite hit (SubSprSprInteract acts as slot 0)

**Codes (all nine are needed):** `CDCF-DDD9` `DDCF-DD09` `6DCF-DD69`
`D7CF-DDA9` `CDC5-D709` `EDC8-DD09` `CDC6-0FA9` `CDC2-07D9` `CDCA-AFA9`
**Raw form:**
- `01A410:A0` (orig `$A8`), `01A411:00` (orig `$45`), `01A412:80` (orig `$13`),
  `01A413:03` (orig `$4A`) — start of `SubSprSprInteract`
- `01A47D:A0` (orig `$15`) — Y test
- `01A4B1:F0` (orig `$30`) — end of the scan loop
- `01A587:A0` (orig `$15`), `01A5DC:A0` (orig `$15`), `01A7C7:A0` (orig `$15`)
  — the touch handlers

(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:29:26

**Mechanism:** Each sprite calls `SubSprSprInteract` with its own slot in X.
The routine puts that slot in Y (the "current" sprite), then walks X down
through the lower slots (the "other" sprite). For each pair that touches, it
calls `CODE_01A4BA`, which picks the result from the two statuses: turn
away, kick, kill, or both die. The handlers get the current sprite back with
`LDY/LDX CurSpriteProcess` in several places.

The codes make slot 0 the current sprite everywhere:
- The start becomes `TXA / BEQ return / LDY #$00 / BRA +3`. Y is 0. The
  `EOR TrueFrame / LSR / BCC` every-other-frame test and the `DEX` are
  skipped, so the scan starts at the caller's own slot.
- The four reads of `CurSpriteProcess` (`$15E9`) inside the scan and its
  handlers now read `$A0E9`. With the data bank set to `$01` (set by
  `ProcessAllSprites`), that is a ROM byte that holds `$00`. So each of them
  gives slot 0.
- The loop end changes `DEX / BMI` to `DEX / BEQ`. The scan stops before
  slot 0, so slot 0 never touches itself.

So when sprite N runs, slot 0 is tested against slots N, N-1, … 1. Anything
that touches the sprite in slot 0 gets the result as if slot 0 had walked
into it. A kicked shell in slot 0 kills whatever it overlaps, for example.
Sprites in slots 1 and up no longer touch each other; they only touch slot 0.
The `LDX CurSpriteProcess` at the end of the scan (`$01A4B6`) is not changed,
so the caller gets its own slot back in X.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `8A F0 FA A8 45 13 4A 90 F4 CA` at `$01A40D`,
`CA 30 03 4C 17 A4 AE E9 15` at `$01A4B0`, and `AC E9 15` / `AE E9 15` at
`$01A47B`, `$01A585`, `$01A5DA` and `$01A7C5`. `$01:A0E9` holds `$00`.
`SubSprSprInteract` is only called with `JSR` from bank 01, under
`ProcessAllSprites` (`PHB / PHK / PLB`). All nine codes round-trip through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Nine codes is more than a real SNES Game Genie holds (5). It works in an
  emulator.
- Slot 0 is the last slot the level loader fills, so it is often empty. Then
  nothing happens: `CODE_01A4BA` returns unless slot 0's status is 8 to `$0B`.
  The effect shows best when many sprites are on screen.
- The scan now runs every frame instead of every other frame, and slot 0 can
  be tested against the same sprite once for each higher slot. Expect more
  slowdown and faster results.
- Uses the same bytes as the next cheat. Do not turn both on.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every sprite bumps only into sprite slot 0 (SubSprSprInteract checks slot 0 only)

**Codes (all four are needed):** `C4CF-DD09` `DDCF-DD69` `6DCF-DDA9` `D4CF-DFD9`
**Raw form:** `01A411:A2` (orig `$45`), `01A412:00` (orig `$13`),
`01A413:80` (orig `$4A`), `01A414:02` (orig `$90`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:29:26

Tags: `interesting` `play-start`

**Mechanism:** Each sprite calls `SubSprSprInteract` with its own slot in X.
The routine keeps that slot in Y (the "current" sprite), then walks X down
through every lower slot (the "other" sprite) and handles each pair that
touches. The codes change the start from
`TAY / EOR TrueFrame / LSR / BCC return / DEX` to
`TAY / LDX #$00 / BRA +2`. X starts at 0, and the loop end (`DEX / BMI`)
exits after that one pass. So each sprite is tested against slot 0 only.
Sprites in slots 1 and up no longer bump, kill or turn each other. Only the
sprite in slot 0 still takes part.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `8A F0 FA A8 45 13 4A 90 F4 CA` at `$01A40D`
(`TXA / BEQ / TAY / EOR $13 / LSR / BCC / DEX`), and `CA 30 03` at `$01A4B0`
(`DEX / BMI`). The codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect
is derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The every-other-frame test is skipped, so each sprite checks slot 0 every
  frame.
- Slot 0 is the last slot the level loader fills, so it is often empty. Then
  sprites do not interact with each other at all. For example, kicked shells
  pass through enemies.
- The sprite in slot 0 itself still returns at once (`TXA / BEQ`), so it
  only takes part when a higher slot runs.
- Uses the same bytes as the previous cheat. Do not turn both on.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Walking enemies kill what they touch (acting sprite always counts as kicked)

**Codes (both are needed):** `8DC8-D7A9` + `09CA-DDD9`
**Raw form:** `01A4BF:B0` (orig `$F0`) + `01A4C0:45` (orig `$0D`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:30:50

**Mechanism:** When two sprites touch, `SubSprSprInteract` calls
`CODE_01A4BA` with Y = the acting sprite (the one whose code is running) and
X = the other sprite. `CODE_01A4BA` reads the acting sprite's status and
branches: `CMP #$08 / BEQ` normal, then `$09` carryable, `$0A` kicked, `$0B`
carried. Any other status returns. The codes change the first branch,
`BEQ CODE_01A4CE` (`F0 0D` at `$01A4BF`), to `BCS CODE_01A506` (`B0 45`).
After `CMP #$08`, carry is set for every status of 8 or more, so all four
active statuses (and anything higher) take the kicked path. The other
sprite's status still counts as normal.

The kicked path uses the other sprite's status:
- Normal: `CODE_01A625` kills it and flings it upward. The acting sprite's
  combo counter (`SpriteMisc1626`) goes up and Mario gets the points.
- Carryable: `CODE_01A642` kills it if it is on the ground. In the air, both
  die (`CODE_01A685`).
- Kicked or carried: both die (`CODE_01A685`).

So two enemies that walk into each other no longer turn around: one of them
dies, as if a shell hit it.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `B9 C8 14 C9 08 F0 0D C9 09 F0 1D C9 0A F0 3D C9
0B F0 4D 60` at `$01A4BA`. `CODE_01A506` is at `$01A506`, so the displacement from
`$01A4C1` is `$45`. Both codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`.
The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in
play**.

**Caveats:**
- Both codes are needed. The second code alone sends only normal sprites to
  a different place and leaves `BEQ`.
- Mario gets points for each kill, and the combo sound rises as one enemy
  kills several.
- A flying `?` block (`$83`/`$84`) is not killed. It gets hit and gives its
  item instead.
- The three "acting sprite counts as ..." cheats use the same two bytes. Turn
  on only one.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Enemies act like dropped shells when they touch (acting sprite always counts as carryable)

**Codes (both are needed):** `8DC8-D7A9` + `4FCA-DDD9`
**Raw form:** `01A4BF:B0` (orig `$F0`) + `01A4C0:21` (orig `$0D`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:30:50

**Mechanism:** When two sprites touch, `SubSprSprInteract` calls
`CODE_01A4BA` with Y = the acting sprite (the one whose code is running) and
X = the other sprite. `CODE_01A4BA` reads the acting sprite's status and
branches: `CMP #$08 / BEQ` normal, then `$09` carryable, `$0A` kicked, `$0B`
carried. Any other status returns. The codes change the first branch,
`BEQ CODE_01A4CE` (`F0 0D` at `$01A4BF`), to `BCS CODE_01A4E2` (`B0 21`).
After `CMP #$08`, carry is set for every status of 8 or more, so all four
active statuses (and anything higher) take the carryable path. The other
sprite's status still counts as normal.

The carryable path first checks if the acting sprite is on the ground:
- In the air: a Goomba (`$0F`) and the other sprite both die. Any other
  sprite takes the kicked path, which kills a normal sprite it touches.
- On the ground (`CODE_01A4F2`): against a normal sprite, `CODE_01A540` runs.
  A shell-less Koopa (a sprite with `SpriteTweakerA` bit `$40`) may kick the
  acting sprite or hop into it, as if it were a shell (`CODE_01A6D9`). Then
  both turn away. A kicked sprite kills it (`CODE_01A5C4`), and a carried
  one makes both die.

So enemies that jump or fall onto others kill them, and shell-less Koopas
treat any enemy standing on the ground as a shell.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `B9 C8 14 C9 08 F0 0D C9 09 F0 1D C9 0A F0 3D C9
0B F0 4D 60` at `$01A4BA`. `CODE_01A4E2` is at `$01A4E2`, so the displacement from
`$01A4C1` is `$21`. Both codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`.
The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in
play**.

**Caveats:**
- Both codes are needed. The second code alone sends only normal sprites to
  a different place and leaves `BEQ`.
- What a shell-less Koopa does when it "enters" a sprite that is not a shell
  has not been traced. Expect glitches.
- The three "acting sprite counts as ..." cheats use the same two bytes. Turn
  on only one.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

**Mechanism:** When two sprites touch, `SubSprSprInteract` calls
`CODE_01A4BA` with Y = the acting sprite (the one whose code is running) and
X = the other sprite. `CODE_01A4BA` reads the acting sprite's status and
branches: `CMP #$08 / BEQ` normal, then `$09` carryable, `$0A` kicked, `$0B`

After `CMP #$08`, carry is set for every status of 8 or more, so all four
active statuses (and anything higher) take the carried path. The other
sprite's status still counts as normal.

The carried path sends every active other sprite (status 8 to `$0B`) to
`CODE_01A685`, where both sprites die and fly apart upward. Mario gets
points (`GivePoints` with 4) each time.

  a different place and leaves `BEQ`.
- Exceptions from `CODE_01A685`: a flying `?` block (`$83`/`$84`) gets hit
  instead of dying, and a key (`$80`) as the acting sprite survives.
- Crowded places can empty fast, and Mario may get many points.
- The three "acting sprite counts as ..." cheats use the same two bytes. Turn
