## Every sprite collides with itself (SubSprSprInteract includes the sprite's own slot)

**Codes:** `3CCF-DF69` + `DDCD-D769`
Optional third code, so sprites touch **only** themselves: `6DC8-DD09`
**Raw form:** `01A416:EA` (orig `$CA`) + `01A40E:00` (orig `$FA`);
optional `01A4B1:80` (orig `$30`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:33:25

**Mechanism:** Each sprite calls `SubSprSprInteract` with its own slot in X.
The routine starts `TXA / BEQ return / TAY / EOR TrueFrame / LSR /
BCC return / DEX`. Y keeps the sprite's own slot, and `DEX` starts the scan
one slot lower, so a sprite never meets itself. The codes do this:
- `3CCF-DF69` changes that `DEX` to `NOP`. The first pair in the scan is now
  the sprite with itself. The scan then goes on down through the lower slots
  as normal.
- `DDCD-D769` changes the `BEQ return` displacement to 0, so slot 0 no longer
  skips the scan and meets itself too. It has no lower slots, so it meets
  nothing else.
- `6DC8-DD09` (optional) changes the loop end `DEX / BMI` to `DEX / BRA`, so
  the scan stops after the first pair. Then each sprite meets only itself.

A sprite always passes the touch test with itself. The fence check passes
too, because `SpriteBehindScene` EOR itself is 0. Then `CODE_01A4BA` runs
with X = Y, and the result comes from the status table with the same status
on both sides:
- **Normal / normal:** `CODE_01A56D` sets the sprite's direction
  (`SpriteMisc157C`) to 1 as the "current" sprite and then to 0 as the
  "other" sprite. So walking enemies without `SpriteTweakerE` bit `$10`
  should keep turning to face right, even after they bump into a wall.
- **Kicked / kicked** and **carried / carried:** `CODE_01A685`, both die. A
  kicked shell or anything Mario holds dies within two frames. Mario gets
  points each time.
- **Carryable / carryable:** on the ground, `CODE_01A555` turns it. In the
  air, a Goomba dies at once, and anything else dies through `CODE_01A642`
  (not on the ground). So a stunned sprite that is thrown or falls dies.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `8A F0 FA A8 45 13 4A 90 F4 CA` at `$01A40D` and
`CA 30 03 4C 17 A4` at `$01A4B0`. `CODE_01A56D` computes the direction with
`SBC` then `ROL / AND #$01`. With equal X positions, carry is set, so it is 1.
All three codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is
derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The check still runs every other frame per slot, as before.
- A sprite with `SpriteTweakerE` bit `$08` (ignores other sprites) or a
  no-contact timer (`SpriteMisc1564`) set is still skipped, so it does not
  meet itself either.
- A flying `?` block (`$83`/`$84`) that meets itself gets hit
  (`CODE_01B4E2`) instead of dying.
- A key (`$80`) as the "current" sprite survives `CODE_01A685`, but as the
  "other" sprite it is killed. So a carried key still dies.
- Carrying anything becomes almost impossible.
- Do not combine this with the slot-0 cheats above. They rewrite the same
  start of the routine, and the optional code uses the same byte
  (`$01A4B1`) as the slot-0 acting cheat.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Each sprite touches only the sprite in the next slot up (SubSprSprInteract scans up by one)

**Codes (all three are needed):** `36CF-DF69` + `6DC8-DD09` + `DDCD-D769`
**Raw form:** `01A416:E8` (orig `$CA`), `01A4B1:80` (orig `$30`),
`01A40E:00` (orig `$FA`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:34:18

**Mechanism:** Each sprite calls `SubSprSprInteract` with its own slot in X.
The routine keeps that slot in Y (the "current" sprite), and `DEX` starts
the scan one slot lower. The loop end (`DEX / BMI`) then walks down to slot
0. So normally a sprite checks **every** lower slot, and each pair is handled
by the higher slot's call. The codes do this:
- `36CF-DF69` changes the first `DEX` to `INX`. The scan starts one slot
  higher.
- `6DC8-DD09` changes the loop end `BMI` to `BRA`, so the scan stops after
  that one pair.
- `DDCD-D769` changes the `BEQ return` displacement to 0, so slot 0 no longer
  skips the scan. It now checks slot 1.

So sprite N is tested only against sprite N+1. Sprites whose slots are two or
more apart pass through each other. Two sprites in neighbouring slots still
bump, kick and kill as usual, but the lower slot is now the "current" sprite
in the status table (`CODE_01A4BA`).

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `8A F0 FA A8 45 13 4A 90 F4 CA` at `$01A40D` and
`CA 30 03 4C 17 A4` at `$01A4B0`. In `rammap.asm`, the 12-byte `SpriteStatus`
table is followed by `SpriteYPosHigh`. All three codes round-trip through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has
not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Slot 11 (the top slot) checks a "slot 12" that does not exist. Its status
  is read from `SpriteYPosHigh` for slot 0. In a normal level that is 0 or 1,
  under 8, so it is skipped. In a vertical level it can be 8 or more. Then
  slot 11 is tested against junk from the next table in RAM, and a kill
  result writes `$02` into slot 0's Y position high byte. Expect glitches
  there.
- The check still runs every other frame per slot.
- Do not combine this with the slot-0 or self-collision cheats above. They
  rewrite the same bytes at the start and end of the scan.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Sprites never skip each other (SubSprSprInteract ignores its skip rules)

**Code:** `DDC7-D409`
**Raw form:** `01A439:00` (orig `$76`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 22:35:36

**Mechanism:** For each pair of active sprites, `SubSprSprInteract` (at
`CODE_01A417`) ORs together the reasons to skip the pair, then
`BNE CODE_01A4B0` goes to the next pair if any is set:
- either sprite has `SpriteTweakerE` bit `$08` (does not touch other
  sprites),
- either sprite has its no-contact timer `SpriteMisc1564` running,
- the other sprite is on Yoshi's tongue (`SpriteOnYoshiTongue`),
- the two are on different sides of a fence (`SpriteBehindScene`).

The code sets that `BNE`'s displacement to 0, so it falls through to the
touch test every time. The status check before it (status under 8 is
skipped) is not changed, so empty and dying slots are still skipped.

Sprites with `SpriteTweakerE` bit `$08` in the U tweaker table
(`Sprite1686Vals`) include the power-ups `$74`–`$78`, the springboard `$2F`,
the P-switch `$3E`, the key `$80` and the platform sprites `$55`–`$5F`. With the
code they bump, turn, kill and are killed like enemies. For example, a kicked
shell should kill a mushroom, and two sprites that should pass through each
other can turn around.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `BD 86 16 19 86 16 29 08 1D 64 15 19 64 15 1D D0
15 1D 32 16 59 32 16 D0 76` at `$01A421`. `D0 76` at `$01A438` branches to
`$01A4B0` (`CODE_01A4B0`). The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has
not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Sprites whose no-contact timer (`SpriteMisc1564`) is running now touch
  others at once. Which sprites set that timer, and when, has not been
  traced here. Expect some instant kills and turn-arounds.
- A sprite on Yoshi's tongue can now kill or be killed by what it passes.
- Sprites on the two sides of a fence touch each other.
- The touch test itself (the X and Y distance) still applies. Sprites must
  overlap to interact.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and the ROM bytes, plus a direct
read of `comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Held shells survive collisions

**Code:** `0CC7-0F09`
**Raw form:** `01A535:4A` (orig `$85`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:14:55

Tags: `demo-ready` `video-ready` `play-start` `curated`

**Mechanism:** When two sprites touch, `CODE_01A4BA` picks the result from
their statuses, with Y = the current sprite and X = the other one. Several
results go through the stub `CODE_01A534: JMP CODE_01A685`, where **both**
sprites die. The code changes that jump's low byte from `$85` to `$4A`, so it
goes to `SprSprKickedKill` (`$01A64A`) instead. Both targets are in page
`$A6`, so one byte is enough.

`SprSprKickedKill` is the code a kicked shell uses to kill a sprite. It takes
X = the victim and Y = the killer:
- it adds 1 to the killer's combo count (`SpriteMisc1626`) and plays the
  stomp sound for that count,
- it gives points at the victim: 200, 400, 800, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, then a
  1-Up for each kill from the 8th on,
- it kills the victim and flings it up and away.

So in every pair that used to end with both sprites dead, only the other
sprite (X) dies, and the current sprite (Y) lives on and builds a combo. The
pairs that used this stub are:
- current normal, other carried
- current carryable in the air and a Goomba (`$0F`), against anything
- current carryable on the ground, other carried
- current kicked, other kicked or carried
- current carried, other anything

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `4C 85 A6` at `$01A534` and `DA B9 26 16` at
`$01A64A` (`SprSprKickedKill`: `PHX / LDA SpriteMisc1626,Y`). The code
round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Which sprite survives depends on the slot order. The current sprite is
  always the one in the higher slot. If Mario's held shell is in the lower
  slot, the enemy is the current sprite, and the held shell dies instead.
- `CODE_01A685`'s exceptions are gone. A flying `?` block (`$83`/`$84`) is now
  killed, not hit, and a key gets no special case.
- The combo count of a carried item keeps growing, so a held shell can earn
  1-Ups.
- Works well with the "Any colliding enemies die" cheat
  (`8DC8-D7A9` + `9BCA-DDD9`). Together, the current sprite in every touching
  pair kills the other and scores a combo.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The name
`SprSprKickedKill` is from the working annotation of `bank_01.asm` and is not
yet in `SMW_U.sym`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Enemies that bump into each other fight, with combo points ("turn away" becomes a kill)

**Codes (both are needed):** `0CC7-0769` + `C1C7-07A9`
**Raw form:** `01A53E:4A` (orig `$6D`) + `01A53F:A6` (orig `$A5`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:14:55

**Mechanism:** When two normal sprites (status 8) touch, `CODE_01A4BA`
branches to the stub `CODE_01A53D: JMP CODE_01A56D`, where both sprites turn
to face away from each other. The codes change the jump target to
`SprSprKickedKill` (`$01A64A`), the code a kicked shell uses to kill a
sprite. It takes X = the victim (the other sprite) and Y = the killer (the
current sprite):
- it adds 1 to the killer's combo count (`SpriteMisc1626`) and plays the
  stomp sound for that count,
- it gives Mario points at the victim: 200, 400, 800, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000,
  then a 1-Up for each kill from the 8th on,
- it kills the victim and flings it up and away.

So when two walking enemies meet, the one in the higher slot kills the other
one, and Mario gets the points.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `4C 6D A5` at `$01A53D` and `DA B9 26 16` at
`$01A64A` (`SprSprKickedKill`). The codes round-trip through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Both codes are needed. With only one of them, the jump goes to `$01A54A`
  or `$01A66D`, which are not the start of any routine.
- Only the normal-vs-normal pair changes. Pairs that reach the turn-away code
  in other ways (carryable sprites on the ground) still turn.
- A flying `?` block (`$83`/`$84`) that touches a normal sprite can be killed.
- The winner's combo count keeps growing, so one busy enemy can earn Mario
  1-Ups. `SpriteMisc1626` is a general-purpose table, so a sprite that uses
  it for something else may start with a count other than 0, and the kill
  also changes that value.
- Can be used together with the "Held shells survive collisions" cheat
  (`0CC7-0F09`). They change different bytes.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The name
`SprSprKickedKill` is from the working annotation of `bank_01.asm` and is not
yet in `SMW_U.sym`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

**Mechanism:** When Mario touches a carryable (stunned, status 9) sprite with
the run button (`byetudlrHold` bit `$40`) held, `CODE_01AA42` picks it up only if
`LDA CarryingFlag / ORA PlayerRidingYoshi` is 0. The springboard
(`SpringBoard`, at `CODE_01E6CE`) has the same gate. `CarryingFlag` is
`$1470`, read as `AD 70 14`. The first two codes change the high byte to
`$81`, so the `LDA` reads `$01:8170`, a ROM byte that holds `$00` (the data
bank is `$01`, set by `ProcessAllSprites`). The gate now tests only
`PlayerRidingYoshi`, so Mario can pick up another item while he holds one,
but still not on Yoshi.

Held items touch each other and nearby sprites, and `CODE_01A4BA` would kill
them: a carried sprite (status `$0B`) that touches anything makes both die.
The other three codes turn off the kills among items Mario is carrying or
about to pick up. Each one sets a `BEQ CODE_01A534` displacement to 0, so it
falls through to the next test and then to `RTS`:
- in `CODE_01A51A` (current sprite carried): the `$0B` test (other carried)
  and the `$09` test (other carryable),
- in `CODE_01A4F2` (current sprite carryable, on the ground): the `$0B` test
  (other carried).

A held item still kills a normal (status 8) enemy it touches, and still dies
with it.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `AD 70 14 0D 7A 18 D0 0E` at `$01AA5E` and
`AD 70 14 0D 7A 18 D0 08` at `$01E6D2`. `$01:8170` holds `$00`.
`CODE_01A51A` is `BD C8 14 C9 08 F0 13 C9 09 F0 0F C9 0A F0 0B C9 0B F0 07 60`
and `CODE_01A4F2` is `BD C8 14 C9 08 F0 47 C9 09 F0 58 C9 0A F0 39 C9 0B F0 2F
60`. All five codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is
derived from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Five codes is the most a real SNES Game Genie holds. Leave out the
  springboard code if you need a slot.
- All held items sit at the same place in Mario's hands, and each one is
  thrown or dropped by its own code when Y is let go. So they should all go
  out together.
- A stunned sprite that is **in the air** still dies with a held item it
  touches (`CODE_01A4E2` sends it to the kicked path). So is a Goomba.
- A held item that meets a kicked shell still dies with it.
- Keys, P-switches, springboards and baby Yoshis do not touch other sprites
  (`SpriteTweakerE` bit `$08`), so they stack without the last three codes.
- The other pick-up paths (throw blocks from the ground in bank 00, and the
  `CarryingFlag` checks at `CODE_01DA0A` and near `CODE_01ED70`) are not
  changed.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Enemies that touch Mario die instead of hurting him (HurtMario becomes a kicked-shell kill)

**Codes (all four are needed):** `B8CF-0FA1` + `0ACF-04D1` + `0CCF-0401` + `C1CF-0461`
**Raw form:** `01A917:9B` (orig `$22`), `01A918:4C` (orig `$B7`),
`01A919:4A` (orig `$F5`), `01A91A:A6` (orig `$00`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:28:45

**Mechanism:** Sprites with the default Mario interaction call
`MarioSprInteract`, which sets the data bank to `$01` and does
`JSR MarioSprInteractRt` with X = the sprite. When Mario touches the sprite
from the side or below, `CODE_01A8E6` ends with `JSL HurtMario`
(`22 B7 F5 00` at `$01A917`). The codes turn those four bytes into
`TXY / JMP SprSprKickedKill` (`9B 4C 4A A6`).

`SprSprKickedKill` (`$01A64A`) is the code a kicked shell uses to kill a
sprite. It needs X = the victim and Y = the killer. `TXY` sets up the enemy
as both, so the enemy "kicks" itself:
- its own combo count (`SpriteMisc1626`) goes up by 1, which is usually from
  0 to 1, so Mario gets 200 points and stomp sound 1,
- it is killed, gets the hit star, and is flung up and in its own direction
  of travel.

Its `RTS` returns from `MarioSprInteractRt`, the same as the `RTS` after
`JSL HurtMario` did.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `B5 9E C9 53 F0 04 22 B7 F5 00 60` at `$01A911`
(`LDA SpriteNumber,X / CMP #$53 / BEQ / JSL HurtMario / RTS`). All four codes
round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Only the default Mario interaction changes. Sprites that call `HurtMario`
  from their own code (`Fish`, `DryBonesAndBeetle`, `WallKoopaKids`,
  `PlatformKoopaKids` in bank 01, and anything in other banks) still hurt
  Mario.
- The throw block (`$53`) is still skipped, and nothing changes while Mario
  is blinking after a hit or riding Yoshi.
- Stomps, spin jumps and sliding kills are not changed.
- A sprite that uses `SpriteMisc1626` for something else can start with a
  count other than 0, which changes the points and sound.
- The contact return value (carry) is not the same as before. The default
  interaction callers did not get a fixed value on this path either.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The name
`SprSprKickedKill` is from the working annotation of `bank_01.asm` and is not
yet in `SMW_U.sym`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## A held item always wins against other sprites, whatever the slot order

**Codes (all four are needed):** `0CC7-0F09` + `91C3-DDD9` + `74CD-0FD9` + `F3CF-04D9`
**Raw form:** `01A535:4A` (orig `$85`), `01A4E0:56` (orig `$53`),
`01A504:32` (orig `$2F`), `01A518:1E` (orig `$1B`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:28:45

**Mechanism:** When two sprites touch, `SprSprContact` (`CODE_01A4BA`) picks
the result from their statuses. Y is the current sprite (the higher slot) and
X is the other one. A carried sprite (status `$0B`) on either side makes both
die, through the stub `CODE_01A534: JMP CODE_01A685`. There are two kill
routines with the same combo points and fling, one for each direction:
- `SprSprKickedKill` (`$01A64A`): X is killed, Y is the killer.
- The code at `CODE_01A5C4`: it swaps the pair, so Y (the current sprite) is
  killed and X is the killer. `CODE_01A537` and `ADDR_01A53A` are
  `JMP CODE_01A5C4` stubs.

The codes route every pair with a carried sprite so that the carried one is
the killer:
- `0CC7-0F09`: `CODE_01A534` jumps to `SprSprKickedKill` instead. This covers
  every pair where the current sprite (Y) is carried: X dies.
- `91C3-DDD9`: current normal vs other carried. `BEQ CODE_01A534` at
  `$01A4DF` goes to `CODE_01A537` instead, so the carried X kills Y.
- `74CD-0FD9`: current carryable on the ground vs other carried. The `BEQ`
  at `$01A503` goes to `CODE_01A537`.
- `F3CF-04D9`: current kicked (or carryable in the air) vs other carried.
  The `BEQ` at `$01A517` goes to `CODE_01A537`.

So a shell in Mario's hands kills every sprite it touches and survives,
with kicked-shell combo points and 1-Ups from the 8th kill. In the original
game, both would die.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `C9 0B F0 53` at `$01A4DD`, `C9 0B F0 2F` at
`$01A501`, `C9 0B F0 1B` at `$01A515` (each `BEQ` lands on `$01A534`), and
`4C 85 A6 4C C4 A5 4C C4 A5` at `$01A534`. All four codes round-trip through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has
not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The first code alone is the "Held shells survive collisions" cheat above. It
  wins only when the held item is in the higher slot. The other three codes
  cover the lower-slot case.
- `CODE_01A685`'s special cases are gone on the first code's pairs. A flying
  `?` block (`$83`/`$84`) touched by a held item from a higher slot is
  killed. `CODE_01A5C4` still hits the block instead.
- A carryable Goomba in the air still goes straight to `CODE_01A534`, so it
  is the killer if it is the current sprite.
- The third code uses the same byte (`$01A504`) as the "carry more than one
  item" cheat. Do not combine them.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The name
`SprSprKickedKill` is from the working annotation of `bank_01.asm` and is not
yet in `SMW_U.sym`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Stomped enemies fly off instead of being squished (smush becomes a kicked-shell kill)

**Codes (all four are needed):** `B8C2-0DA1` + `0AC2-0FD1` + `0CC2-0F01` + `C1C2-0F61`
**Raw form:** `01A9D3:9B` (orig `$A9`), `01A9D4:4C` (orig `$03`),
`01A9D5:4A` (orig `$9D`), `01A9D6:A6` (orig `$C8`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:28:45

**Mechanism:** When Mario stomps a sprite that is squished by a stomp,
`MarioSprInteractRt` reaches `CODE_01A9D3`: `LDA #$03 / STA SpriteStatus,X`
(smushed), then a timer and zero speed. The codes turn the first four bytes
into `TXY / JMP SprSprKickedKill`. Y is the sprite number at this point
(`LDY SpriteNumber,X` in `CODE_01A95D`), not a slot, so `TXY` is needed to
set up the sprite itself as the killer. `SprSprKickedKill` then kills the
sprite, flings it up and in its own direction of travel, and gives
kicked-shell points from its own combo count (`SpriteMisc1626`).

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 03 9D C8 14 A9 20 9D 40 15` at `$01A9D3`. All
four codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived
from the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The stomp points from `CODE_01AB46` are still given first, so each stomp
  also gives the kick-kill points (usually 200 more).
- Only the smush result changes. Sprites that fall straight down, lose their
  wings, or turn into a shell-less Koopa are not changed.
- Sprites `$04`–`$10` (Koopas and Goombas) that are stomped while
  `FlightPhase` is non-zero also reach this code, so they fly off too.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym` and a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header. The name
`SprSprKickedKill` is from the working annotation of `bank_01.asm` and is not
yet in `SMW_U.sym`.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Stomped winged Goombas become Bob-ombs (SpriteToSpawn read 2 bytes later)

**Code:** `A8CB-0401`
**Raw form:** `01A999:CB` (orig `$C9`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:35:40

**Mechanism:** When Mario stomps a winged Koopa (`$08`–`$0C`) or a winged
Goomba (`$10`), `MarioSprInteractRt` reaches `CODE_01A998`:
`LDA.W SpriteToSpawn,Y` with Y = the sprite number. `SpriteToSpawn` is at
`$01A7C9`, so the instruction is `B9 C9 A7`. `CODE_01A99B` stores the result
as the new sprite number and runs `LoadSpriteTables`. The code changes the
operand's low byte from `$C9` to `$CB`, so the table is read from `$01A7CB`
instead. That is 2 bytes later, so every winged sprite reads a
different byte and becomes a different sprite:

| Stomped sprite | Becomes |
|---|---|
| $08 Green Koopa, flying left | $05 Red Koopa |
| $09 Green bouncing Koopa | $05 Red Koopa |
| $0A Red vertical flying Koopa | $07 Yellow Koopa |
| $0B Red horizontal flying Koopa | $00 Green Koopa, no shell |
| $0C Yellow Koopa with wings | $00 Green Koopa, no shell |
| $10 Bouncing Goomba with wings | $0D Bob-omb |

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `B9 C9 A7` at `$01A998`. The bytes read are
`05 05 07 00 00 0D` at `$01A7CB+Y` for Y = `$08`–`$0C` and `$10`. The sprite names are
from the sprite pointer table in `bank_01.asm`. The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has
not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The Koopas also change colour, and some come out without a shell.
- Only this stomp reader moves. Yoshi's mouth (`CODE_01F344`) and the other
  `SpriteToSpawn` readers still read the real table.
- The Para-Goomba (`$3F`) and Para-Bomb (`$40`) use a different read
  (`SpriteToSpawn2-$40,Y`) and are not changed.
- `LoadSpriteTables` sets the new sprite's tweakers, but its init routine
  does not run, and the status stays 8. Sprites that need their init may act
  oddly.
- The three `SpriteToSpawn` shift cheats all use this one byte (`$01A999`). Turn on only one.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Star power kills the wrong sprite (star kill writes to slot StarKillCounter)

**Code:** `BBC1-D7D1`
**Raw form:** `01A86C:99` (orig `$9D`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-18 23:43:37

**Mechanism:** `MarioSprInteractRt` (`ProcessInteract`) handles Mario
touching a sprite, with X = that sprite. When Mario has a star, or slides into
a sprite, it runs the star-kill code at `CODE_01A847`:
1. hit star and kick sound at the sprite (`CODE_01AB6F`),
2. `INC StarKillCounter` (capped at 8) and `GivePoints` with it,
3. `LDY StarKillCounter` to pick the stomp sound,
4. `LDA #$02 / STA SpriteStatus,X`: the sprite is killed,
5. Y speed `$D0` and an X speed away from Mario.

X can't be changed here. `ProcessAllSprites` walks the slots with X
(`DEX / BPL`), so a changed X would break the sprite loop. Instead, the code
changes step 4's `STA SpriteStatus,X` (`9D C8 14`) to `STA SpriteStatus,Y`
(`99 C8 14`). Y still holds `StarKillCounter`, so the "killed" status goes to
**slot 1, 2, 3 … 8** in turn, not to the sprite Mario touched.

What that should look like:
- The touched enemy gets the hit star, the points and the fling speed, but it
  stays alive (status 8). It bounces away and can be touched again.
- Whatever is in slot N falls off the screen as killed. If slot N is the
  touched sprite, it dies as normal.
- If slot N is empty, status 2 brings back the old sprite that last used the
  slot, and it falls off the screen.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `AC D2 18 C0 08 B0 06 B9 1D A6 8D F9 1D A9 02 9D
C8 14` at `$01A85E` (`LDY StarKillCounter / CPY #$08 / BCS / LDA
StompSFX-1,Y / STA SPCIO0 / LDA #$02 / STA SpriteStatus,X`). Nothing between
the `LDY` and the `STA` changes Y. `GivePoints` adds 5 to the count, so a
count of 8 is score sprite `$0D`, a 1-Up. The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has
not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Nothing sets the no-contact timer on this path, and the touched enemy does
  not die, so Mario can hit the same enemy again two frames later. The count
  goes up on each hit. Once it reaches 8, every hit gives a **1-Up**. Holding
  a star against one enemy can give a lot of lives.
- `StarKillCounter` is only reset when Mario touches a sprite without a star,
  so the count carries over between enemies during one star.
- The sliding kill (`CODE_01A8E6`, `PlayerSlopePose`) uses the same code, so
  sliding into enemies does the same without a star.
- Slot 0 is never hit, because the count is at least 1. Slots 9–11 are never
  hit either, because it stops at 8.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Mario's touch hits the next enemy (ProcessInteract moves to slot X-1)

**Code:** `ACC5-D761`
**Raw form:** `01A87E:CA` (orig `$9C`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 00:00:43

**Mechanism:** `MarioSprInteractRt` checks whether Mario touches the sprite
in slot X. If he does, and he has no star, it goes to `CODE_01A87E`. That
code decides what happens: a stomp, a spin-jump kill, a hurt, a kick of a
stunned shell, or a pick-up.

`CODE_01A87E` starts with `STZ StarKillCounter` (`9C D2 18`). The code
changes `$9C` to `$CA`, which is `DEX`. The two bytes after it now read as
`CMP ($18)`, which only sets flags, and the next `LDA` sets them again. So the
touch test still uses the enemy Mario touched, but everything after it
uses **slot X-1**, the slot the sprite loop runs next.

What that should look like:
- Mario stomps an enemy. He bounces, but the enemy in the next slot is the one
  that gets squashed or turned into a shell.
- The result also depends on the other enemy. If Mario stomps a Goomba and
  the next slot holds a Spiny, the game hurts Mario, because a Spiny can't
  be stomped.
- Mario runs into an enemy and gets hurt, but the enemy in the next slot turns
  to face him.
- Mario touches a stunned shell, and the item in the next slot is kicked or
  picked up.
- The touched enemy gets no no-contact timer, so it can hit Mario again on
  the next check.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `9C D2 18 BD 4C 15` at `$01A87E` (`STZ
StarKillCounter / LDA SpriteMisc154C,X`). `$18` is `axlr0000Frame` and `$19` is
`Powerup` (0–3), so `CMP ($18)` reads one byte from `$0000`–`$03FF` of bank
`$01`, which is low RAM. Nothing else jumps into the middle of these 3 bytes.
The code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from
the disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- X stays at X-1 after the routine returns, so the rest of that sprite's code
  for that frame (movement, graphics) runs on slot X-1. The sprite loop then
  counts down from X-1, so slot X-1 does not get its own full turn that
  frame. Expect a one-frame flicker or jump.
- If Mario touches the sprite in slot 0, X becomes `$FF`, and the result
  writes past the end of the sprite tables into other RAM. The sprite loop
  then stops for that frame.
- If the next slot is empty, the result goes to an empty slot. A stomp can
  bring back the old sprite from that slot.
- A star kill does not go through `CODE_01A87E`, so a star still kills the
  enemy that was touched. For star kills that also hit the wrong sprite, see
  `BBC1-D7D1`.
- `StarKillCounter` is no longer reset on a normal touch. This matters only
  with `BBC1-D7D1` or a star.
- Sprites with their own Mario interaction (`SpriteTweakerD` bit 7) return
  before this code and are not affected.

`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

checked.

## Mario always touches every enemy (ProcessInteract contact tests always pass)

**Codes:** `DDCD-DD61` + `DDCD-D761` + `DDC7-DD01`
**Raw form:** `01A802:00` (orig `$F2`), `01A80E:00` (orig `$E6`),
`01A831:00` (orig `$4A`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 00:00:43

**Mechanism:** `ProcessInteract` has three tests that decide whether Mario
touches the sprite in slot X:
1. `SubHorizPos`, then `ADC #$50 / CMP #$A0 / BCS` (no touch if Mario is more
   than `$50` pixels away left or right),
2. `CODE_01AD42`, then `ADC #$60 / CMP #$C0 / BCS` (no touch if more than
   `$60` pixels away up or down),
3. `GetMarioClipping` / `GetSpriteClippingA` / `CheckForContact`, then
   `BCC ReturnNoContact2` (no touch if the boxes don't overlap).

Each code sets one branch offset to `$00`. The branch then goes to the next
instruction whether it is taken or not, so all three tests always pass. Every
sprite that runs this routine acts as if Mario is touching it.

What that should look like:
- With a star, every enemy on the screen dies as soon as it runs this check.
- Without a star, the result depends on Mario's height. `CODE_01A87E` compares
  Mario's Y position with the sprite's box, so an enemy below a falling Mario
  is stomped, and an enemy level with or above Mario hurts him.
- Carryable items (status 9) are kicked or picked up from across the screen.
- Each sprite then waits 8 frames (`SpriteMisc154C`) before it can touch Mario
  again. Hurt i-frames (`IFrameTimer`) are the only protection against enemies
  hurting Mario, so expect Mario to lose his power-up and then die quickly on
  most screens.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `B0 F2` at `$01A801`, `B0 E6` at `$01A80D` and
`90 4A` at `$01A830`, right after the three tests above. The codes round-trip
through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and
**has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Tests that are not about position still apply. A sprite that is off screen
  (unless `SpriteTweakerD` bit 5 is set), a sprite on the other side of a net,
  and any sprite during a Mario animation (`PlayerAnimation` ≥ 1) are still
  skipped.
- Sprites with their own Mario interaction (`SpriteTweakerD` bit 7) get carry
  set every time. What they do with it depends on each sprite's code.
- All three codes are needed for the full effect. With only the first two,
  the box test still decides, so play looks normal. With only `DDC7-DD01`,
  the range tests still hold, so Mario touches every enemy within about
  `$50` pixels left or right and `$60` pixels up or down. This is a milder
  form of the cheat.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Stomp from any height (MarioSprDefaultContact skips the height test)

**Code:** `DDCC-D7A1`
**Raw form:** `01A8AF:00` (orig `$36`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 00:25:15

**Mechanism:** `MarioSprDefaultContact` (`$01A87E`) decides what happens when
Mario touches a normal sprite without a star. A sprite is stomped only if
all three tests pass:
1. Mario's Y position is at least `$14` pixels above the top of the sprite's
   hit box,
2. Mario is falling, or the sprite can be stomped while he rises
   (`SpriteTweakerF` bit 4), or he is in a stomp chain (`SpriteStompCounter`),
3. the sprite is in the air, or Mario is in the air.

If any test fails, the sprite hurts Mario (`CODE_01A8E6`).

Test 1 ends in `BMI CODE_01A8E6` (`30 36`). The code sets the branch offset
to `$00`, so taken or not, it goes on to the next instruction. The height
test no longer matters. Tests 2 and 3 still decide.

What that should look like:
- Mario falls or jumps down onto an enemy from the side or from below its
  top. It is stomped, not hurting him.
- Mario walks on the ground into an enemy that is in the air, such as a
  Paratroopa or a jumping fish. On the ground his Y speed is not negative, so
  test 2 passes, and test 3 passes because the enemy is in the air. The
  enemy is stomped.
- Right after a stomp, while the stomp chain is running, Mario can jump up
  into an enemy from below and stomp it.
- An enemy that can't be jumped on (a Spiny, for example) still hurts him,
  unless he is spin-jumping or riding Yoshi.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 14 85 01 A5 05 38 E5 01 26 00 C5 D3 08 46 00
A5 0B E9 00 28 E5 D4 30 36` at `$01A897`. That is the 16-bit compare of
`_5`/`_B` minus `$14` against `PlayerYPosNow`, ending in the `BMI`. The
branch target `$01A8E6` is `$01A8B0 + $36`. The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Mario walking on the ground into an enemy that is also on the ground still
  gets hurt (test 3).
- Mario jumping up into an enemy still gets hurt, unless he is in a stomp
  chain or the sprite can be stomped while he rises (test 2).
- After a stomp from the side, the game bounces Mario up and may place him
  on the sprite in the usual way. Where he ends up has not been checked.
- Only sprites that use the default Mario touch code are affected. Sprites
  with their own touch code (`SpriteTweakerD` bit 7) are not.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Touch every frame (MarioSprDefaultContact ignores the no-contact timer)

**Code:** `DDC6-DF01`
**Raw form:** `01A885:00` (orig `$0F`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 00:26:40

**Mechanism:** `MarioSprDefaultContact` (`$01A87E`) starts with
`LDA SpriteMisc154C,X / BNE CODE_01A895` (`BD 4C 15 D0 0F`). If the sprite's
no-contact timer is still running, the touch is ignored. Otherwise the code
sets the timer to 8 and handles the touch. Other code sets the timer too.
A kick (`CODE_01AA97`) sets it to `$10`, so the shell Mario just kicked
can't touch him.

The code sets the branch offset to `$00`, so the branch goes to the next
instruction whether it is taken or not. The timer is still set, but it no
longer blocks anything. Each touch is handled every time the check runs:
every frame for sprites with `SpriteTweakerD` bit 5, and every other frame
for the rest.

What that should look like:
- A stomp can hit the same enemy again a few frames later. `CODE_01AB46`
  adds to `SpriteStompCounter` on each stomp, and test 2 of the stomp check
  passes while that counter is set, even if Mario is rising. So one jump can
  stomp an enemy several times and score several combo points. A Koopa can go
  from winged to shell to kicked shell in one landing.
- A stunned enemy (status 9) that Mario lands on is kicked or picked up at
  once, on the next check.
- A shell Mario just kicked is no longer protected by its `$10` timer. If it
  is still touching him on the next check, it can hurt him.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `9C D2 18 BD 4C 15 D0 0F A9 08 9D 4C 15` at
`$01A87E`, and `A9 10 9D 4C 15` in the kick code at `CODE_01AA97`. The code
round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The hurt path still honors `IFrameTimer`, so a sprite that hurts Mario
  can't hurt him again while he flashes.
- `SpriteMisc154C` is also read by other code (36 uses in bank 01). This code
  only changes the check in `MarioSprDefaultContact`.
- Whether a freshly kicked shell hurts Mario depends on the shell's own code
  sending it here while it still overlaps him. That path was not traced.
- Only sprites that use the default Mario touch code are affected.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Power-ups, coins don't disappear when touched

**Code:** `7AAA-DF69`
**Raw form:** `01C4C6:3C` (orig `$9E`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 00:42:53

Tags: `interesting` `play-start`

**Mechanism:** Power-ups (`$74`–`$78`) and sprite coins (`$21`) check for
Mario in `CODE_01C4AC`, from `PowerUpRt` and from the feather's code. On a
touch, `CODE_01C4BF` does `STZ SpriteStatus,X` (`9E C8 14`) to remove the
item. Then it goes to `TouchedPowerUp`, which gives the power-up, the 1-Up,
the item-box item and the points, or goes to the coin code.

The code changes `$9E` (`STZ abs,X`) to `$3C` (`BIT abs,X`). `BIT` only reads,
and the next `LDA SpriteNumber,X` sets the flags again. So the item gives
its effect as normal, but it stays.

Nothing in this path sets a no-contact timer, so the touch repeats while Mario
stays on the item:
- **1-Up mushroom:** a 1-Up on every check, which is every frame or every
  other frame. Standing on one fills the lives counter very fast.
- **Mushroom:** small Mario grows. Mario's growing animation blocks all touches
  (`PlayerAnimation` ≥ 1). After that he is already big, so each touch gives
  1000 points (`CODE_01C56F`), unless the item came from the item box
  (`SpriteMisc1534`).
- **Fire flower / feather:** Mario gets the power, and the item box may fill.
  The feather starts Mario's cape animation, which blocks touches for `$18`
  frames each time. The flower goes on giving 1000 points.
- **Star:** each touch starts the star timer again, so Mario keeps star power
  while he stays on it.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `BD 4C 15 D0 3B BD 40 15 C9 18 B0 34 9E C8 14 B5 9E
C9 21` at `$01C4BA` (`LDA SpriteMisc154C,X / BNE / LDA SpriteMisc1540,X / CMP
#$18 / BCS / STZ SpriteStatus,X / LDA SpriteNumber,X / CMP #$21`). The code
round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Sprite coins (`$21`) use the same code, so they stay too and give a coin on
  every touch.
- The same `STZ` serves 1-Ups and the other power-ups, so one code covers both.
  There is no separate 1-Up-only code at one byte.
- Yoshi eating an item is not affected. Yoshi's code (`CODE_01F373`) sets the
  status to 0 itself before it calls `CODE_01C4BF`.
- The item's sound plays on every touch.
- Lives stop at the game's normal cap. Points may reach the score cap.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Enemies ignore Mario for a second after a touch (no-contact timer 8 → 60)

**Code:** `7AC6-DFA1`
**Raw form:** `01A887:3C` (orig `$08`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 00:46:29

**Mechanism:** `MarioSprDefaultContact` (`$01A87E`) handles a touch only if
the sprite's no-contact timer `SpriteMisc154C` is 0. It then sets the timer
with `LDA #$08 / STA SpriteMisc154C,X` (`A9 08 9D 4C 15`). `CODE_0180D2`
counts the timer down by one each frame (not while sprites are locked). So
each sprite handles Mario's touch at most once every 8 frames.

The code changes the `#$08` to `#$3C`. Each sprite now handles a touch at most
once every **60 frames**, about one second.

What that should look like:
- After Mario stomps an enemy, it ignores him for a second. A stomped Goomba
  or a shell (status 9) can't be kicked or picked up at once. Mario passes
  through it until the timer runs out.
- An enemy that hurt Mario can't touch him again for a second. His flashing
  after a hit lasts longer than that, so nothing changes there.
- A stomp chain can't hit the same enemy twice within the second.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `9C D2 18 BD 4C 15 D0 0F A9 08 9D 4C 15` at
`$01A87E`. The immediate is at `$01A887`. The code round-trips through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has not
been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Only this setting of the timer changes. A kick (`CODE_01AA97`) sets it to
  `$10` right after, so a kicked shell still waits only 16 frames. Other sprite
  code that sets `SpriteMisc154C` keeps its own values.
- Star kills and sprites with their own touch code (`SpriteTweakerD` bit 7) do
  not use this timer.
- With `DDC6-DF01` (touch every frame), the timer is ignored, so this code
  does nothing.

## Stomps don't hurt enemies

**Codes:** `1DC0-0461` (plus `6DC4-0D61` for spin jumps and Yoshi)
**Raw form:** `01A94A:60` (orig `$BD`); `01A922:80` (orig `$F0`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-19 01:11:10

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `challenge`

**Mechanism:** When Mario stomps a sprite that can be jumped on,
`MarioSprDefaultContact` goes to `CODE_01A91C`:
- `LDA SpinJumpFlag / ORA PlayerRidingYoshi / BEQ CODE_01A947`. On a spin
  jump or on Yoshi it falls through to `CODE_01A924`, the spin kill.
- `CODE_01A947` is the plain stomp. `JSR CODE_01A8D8` plays the splat sound,
  bounces Mario (`BoostMarioSpeed`) and shows the hit star. Then
  `LDA SpriteMisc187B,X / BEQ CODE_01A95D`, and `CODE_01A95D` does the damage:
  points and the stomp chain (`CODE_01AB46`), then the change to the next
  form (`SpriteToSpawn`), the smush, the fall, or the stun.

`1DC0-0461` changes the `LDA SpriteMisc187B,X` opcode (`$BD`) to `$60`
(`RTS`). The stomp now ends right after the bounce. Mario bounces with the
splat sound and the hit star, and the enemy is not changed at all.

`6DC4-0D61` changes the `BEQ` at `$01A922` to `BRA` (`$80`), so spin jumps and
stomps while riding Yoshi also take the plain-stomp path, and are harmless too.
Without it, spin jumps and Yoshi stomps still kill.

What that should look like:
- Mario can bounce on Goombas, Koopas and other enemies forever. They keep
  walking, and he gets no points.
- A winged Koopa keeps its wings. A Koopa stays in its shell.
- The stomp chain doesn't grow, because `CODE_01AB46` is skipped.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `20 D8 A8 BD 7B 18 F0 0E` at `$01A947`, and `AD 0D
14 0D 7A 18 F0 23` at `$01A91C` (`$01A924 + $23 = $01A947`). Both codes
round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- The skipped `SpriteMisc187B` branch was the only other thing after the
  bounce. It pushed Mario sideways off some sprites. That push is gone too.
- Spin-jumping onto a carryable item (status 9) goes to `CODE_01A924` by a
  `JMP` from `CODE_01AA42`, not through `$01A922`, so those items still die.
- Enemies that can't be jumped on still hurt Mario, as before. Star kills,
  shells, fireballs and cape hits still work.
- The enemy's no-contact timer is still set, so Mario gets 8 frames before the
  same enemy can touch him again. If he lands beside it rather than on it
  after the bounce, it can hurt him.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## The reserve item drops as a Yoshi egg

**Codes:** `4860-D466` + `DF60-DDA6`
**Raw form:** `02804A:2B` (orig `$73`); `028043:01` (orig `$08`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-29 13:42:22

**Mechanism:** When the reserve item drops (a Select press, or when Mario is
hurt), `CODE_028008` (`bank_02.asm`) spawns it as a sprite:

```
CODE_028042:
    LDA.B #$08                                ; \ Sprite status = Normal
    STA.W SpriteStatus,X                      ; /
    PLA
    CLC
    ADC.B #$73
    STA.B SpriteNumber,X
```

`PLA` gives the old `PlayerItembox` value: 1 mushroom, 2 fire flower, 3 star,
4 feather. `ADC #$73` turns it into sprite `$74`-`$77`.

`4860-D466` changes the `ADC` operand to `$2B`. A mushroom becomes sprite
`$2C`, the Yoshi egg.

`DF60-DDA6` changes the status from `$08` (normal) to `$01` (init). A new
sprite with status `$08` does not run its init routine. The egg needs its init:
`InitYoshiEgg` sets `SpriteMisc187B`, which makes the egg wait for Mario.
Status `$01` sends the sprite to `CallSpriteInit`, which runs `InitYoshiEgg`
and then sets status `$08`.

What that should look like:
- The egg appears where the item normally appears, near the top middle of the
  screen. It does not fall, because `YoshiEgg` does not move the sprite.
- When Mario comes within `$20` pixels to the left or right, the egg hatches.
  It hatches into a baby Yoshi (`$2D`), or into a 1-up (`$78`) if
  `YoshiIsLoose` is set. This is the same test as an egg from a block.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 08 9D C8 14 68 18 69 73` at `$028042`. Both
codes round-trip through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- **The other items change too**, because they use the same `ADC`. A fire
  flower becomes `$2D` (baby Yoshi), a star becomes `$2E` (Spike Top), and a
  feather becomes `$2F` (springboard). `InitKey_BabyYoshi` makes the baby Yoshi
  carryable, so it falls. The Spike Top and the springboard spawn in the air
  at the top of the screen.
- With `4860-D466` only, the egg skips its init. `SpriteMisc187B` and
  `SpriteMisc1540` are both 0, so `YoshiEgg` hatches it on its first frame.
  `CODE_01F83D` then sets the sprite number to `SpriteMisc151C`, which is 0.
  So the egg breaks at once into a shell-less green Koopa (`$00`) with no init.
  It is a different effect, and not a Yoshi egg you can see.
- If Mario stays far from the middle of the screen, the egg can scroll off
  screen before it hatches. `YoshiEgg` does not hatch it while it is off
  screen.
- `CODE_028008` still does `INC SpriteMisc1534,X` after the spawn. That flag
  makes a normal item fall slowly. The egg's code does not read it, and the
  hatch clears it with `InitSpriteTables`.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Every stomp is a Yoshi stomp (enemies vanish in a puff of smoke)

**Codes:** `DDC4-0DA1` + `DDC7-0DD1`
**Raw form:** `01A923:00` (orig `$23`); `01A930:00` (orig `$04`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-29 14:43:08

**Mechanism:** When Mario lands on a sprite that can be jumped on,
`MarioSprInteractRt` goes to `CODE_01A91C`:

```
CODE_01A91C:
    LDA.W SpinJumpFlag
    ORA.W PlayerRidingYoshi
    BEQ CODE_01A947
CODE_01A924:
    JSL DisplayContactGfx
    LDA.B #$F8
    STA.B PlayerYSpeed+1
    LDA.W PlayerRidingYoshi
    BEQ +
    JSL BoostMarioSpeed
  + JSR CODE_019ACB
    ...
```

A plain stomp takes the `BEQ` to `CODE_01A947`. A spin jump or a stomp on
Yoshi falls through to `CODE_01A924`. There `CODE_019ACB` sets status `$04`
(killed by a spin jump), so the sprite turns into a puff of smoke.
`CODE_07FC3B` shows the spin-kill stars, `CODE_01AB46` gives the points, and
the spin-kill sound plays. On Yoshi, `BoostMarioSpeed` also gives Mario a
full stomp bounce (`$D0`, or `$A8` if B is held).

`DDC4-0DA1` changes the `BEQ` displacement from `$23` to `$00`. The branch
now goes to the next instruction either way, so every stomp runs the Yoshi and
spin-jump kill.

`DDC7-0DD1` changes the displacement of `BEQ +` from `$04` to `$00`, so
`BoostMarioSpeed` runs even when Mario is not on Yoshi. Without it, a plain
stomp gets only the small `$F8` hop that a spin jump gets.

What that should look like:
- Every enemy that can be stomped disappears in a puff of smoke, with the
  spin-kill sound and stars.
- Koopas don't lose their shells, and winged enemies don't lose their wings.
  `SpriteToSpawn` is in `CODE_01A95D`, which no longer runs.
- Mario bounces as high as a normal stomp, and higher if he holds B.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `AD 0D 14 0D 7A 18 F0 23` at `$01A91C` and `AD 7A
18 F0 04 22 33 AA 01` at `$01A92C`. Both codes round-trip through
`tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the disassembly and **has
not been observed in play**.

**Alternatives:**

| Codes | Effect |
|---|---|
| `DDC4-0DA1` | every stomp kills in a puff of smoke, but Mario only gets the small spin-jump hop |

**Caveats:**
- With `DDC7-0DD1`, spin-jump kills also give the full bounce, as they would
  on Yoshi.
- Enemies that can't be jumped on (Spinies, and so on) still hurt Mario. A
  spin jump still bounces off them, as before.
- `CODE_01A95D` also had special cases: a stomped Dino-Rhino (`$6E`) became
  a Dino-Torch, and a stomped Super Koopa (`$72` and up) ran `CODE_02EAF2`
  to spawn another sprite. They are skipped, so those sprites vanish in smoke
  as well.
- `CODE_01A947` is not used any more. Its sideways push off some sprites
  (the `SpriteMisc187B` case) is gone.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.

Addresses verified for the U release; the other four releases have not been
checked.

## Spin-jumping on turn blocks drills straight down through them

**Code:** `6565-AF6B`
**Raw form:** `028776:87` (orig `$7D`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-29 17:29:25

**Mechanism:** When big Mario spin-jumps onto a turn block, `CODE_00EE57`
(`bank_00.asm`) sees tile `$1E` under his feet and calls
`HandleFunctionalBlockByID` with block `$21`. Entry `$21` of
`IntBlk_BounceSprite` is `$07`, the only `$07` in that table, so
`CODE_028752` (`bank_02.asm`) takes its shatter path:

```
  + LDA.B #$D0                                ; Deflect Mario downward
    STA.B PlayerYSpeed+1                      ; /
    LDA.B #$00                                ; for shatter routine?
    JSL ShatterBlock                          ; Actually break the block
```

The comment is wrong about the direction. `$D0` is -48, and a negative Y
speed moves up, so this is the bounce that throws Mario up off the block he
just broke.

The code changes the `STA` operand from `$7D` (`PlayerYSpeed+1`) to `$87`.
`rammap.asm` lists `$7E0087` as unused. The `$D0` now goes nowhere, and
Mario's Y speed stays as it was: falling. The block still breaks and gives
its points. With nothing under him, Mario keeps falling onto the next block.
If that is also a turn block and he is still spin-jumping, it breaks too.

What that should look like:
- Big Mario spin-jumps onto a stack of turn blocks and breaks straight down
  through it, one block after another, without bouncing.

**Evidence:** The ROM holds `A9 D0 85 7D A9 00 22 63 86 02` at `$028773`. The
code round-trips through `tools/gg_encode.py`. The effect is derived from the
disassembly and **has not been observed in play**.

**Caveats:**
- Only the spin-jump shatter is changed. Hitting a turn block from below
  still makes it spin, and small Mario still can't break turn blocks.
- The bounce was what kept Mario above the broken block. Over a pit, or
  over a turn block with nothing under it, he falls.
- `ShatterBlock` is also called by a charging Chargin' Chuck and by other
  sprites. Those calls don't go through this store, so they don't change.

**Provenance:** Addresses from `SMW_U.sym`, plus a direct read of
`comparison_U.smc` minus its 512-byte copier header.
