Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `video-ready`

**Mechanism:** This is the same as "Mario throws Yoshi fireballs", except
for the X speed code. This one changes the low byte of the
table's address in `LDA.W DATA_00FE94,Y` (`B9 94 FE` at `$00FECB`), so it
reads `$00FE2D,Y`. Those two bytes are code in `CODE_00FE16`, `97 69`. As
speeds, that is `$97` (-6.6 px per frame) facing left and `$69` (+6.6 px per
frame) facing right. Both directions get the same speed, but it is more than
2.5 times Yoshi's `$28`.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `B9 94 FE` at `$00FECB` and `97 69` at
`$00FE2D`. The codes decode back to their raw forms with
`tools/gg_encode.py`.

**Caveats:**

- `ProcessFireball` checks each slot only every 4th frame, so the fireball
  moves about 26 px between checks. It can fly past small enemies.
- The other caveats of "Mario throws Yoshi fireballs" apply.
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Stomps launch Mario very high

**Codes:** `CBC2-D701` `6DC2-D761` `69C2-D7A1` `52C3-DDD1`
**Raw form:** `01A8DD:A9` (orig `$22`); `01A8DE:80` (orig `$33`);
`01A8DF:85` (orig `$AA`); `01A8E0:7D` (orig `$01`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-04 22:41:30

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `stomp-collection` `video-ready`

**Mechanism:** `CODE_01A8D8` (`bank_01.asm`) plays the splat sound and bounces
Mario up after a normal stomp. Its `JSL BoostMarioSpeed` gives Y speed `$D0`,
or `$A8` if B is held:

```
CODE_01A8D8:
    LDA.B #!SFX_SPLAT
    STA.W SPCIO0
    JSL BoostMarioSpeed       ; 22 33 AA 01 at $01A8DD
    JSL DisplayContactGfx
    RTS
```

The codes replace the 4-byte `JSL` with `LDA.B #$80 / STA.B PlayerYSpeed+1`
(`A9 80 85 7D`), also 4 bytes. `$80` is the fastest upward speed, so every
normal stomp launches Mario far higher than a usual bounce.

Stomping a Chuck does not bounce Mario higher than other enemies. `CODE_02C79D`
calls the same `BoostMarioSpeed`.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `A9 02 8D F9 1D 22 33 AA 01 22 99 AB 01
60` at `$01A8D8`, as in the source. The codes decode back to their raw forms
with `tools/gg_encode.py`.

**Caveats:**

- Holding B makes no difference.
- `CODE_01A8D8` also runs when Mario spin jumps or rides Yoshi onto an enemy
  that cannot be stomped (`CODE_01A8C9` falls into it). That bounce is a
  launch too.
- Spin-jump kills, Chucks, bosses and other enemies call `BoostMarioSpeed`
  directly, so their bounce does not change.
- The `PlayerIsClimbing` check in `BoostMarioSpeed` is skipped.
- Works with "Stomping an enemy knocks Mario off to the side" (6 codes
  together, so emulator only).
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Small and big Mario throw fireballs

**Codes:** `DD26-DFDD`
**Raw form:** `00D084:00` (orig `$28`) (address:new-byte — the original byte is
documentation, not part of the code; SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-05 21:18:34

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `video-ready` `curated`

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00D062` (`bank_00.asm`) handles the X/Y button for the
cape and the fire flower. It runs every frame on land (from `CODE_00CD82`) and
in water (from `CODE_00DA7C`). Cape Mario goes to the cape spin code. Every
other power-up falls into `CODE_00D081`:

```
CODE_00D081:
    CMP.B #$03                ; C9 03 at $00D081
    BNE Return00D0AD          ; D0 28 at $00D083
    LDA.B PlayerIsDucking
    ORA.W PlayerRidingYoshi
    BNE Return00D0AD
    BIT.B byetudlrFrame
    BVS CODE_00D0AA
    ...
CODE_00D0AA:
    JSR ShootFireball
```

The code sets the `BNE` displacement to `$00`. A branch of zero lands on the
next instruction, so both outcomes go on to the fire code, and small and big
Mario shoot fireballs on a new X/Y press. `ShootFireball` itself does not check
the power-up.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `CODE_00D081` at `$00D081` and
`Return00D0AD` at `$00D0AD`. The reference ROM has `C9 03 D0 28` at
`$00D081`, and `$00D085 + $28 = $00D0AD`. The code decodes back to its raw
form with `tools/gg_encode.py`.

**Caveats:**

- Cape Mario still gets the cape spin and no fireballs. Fire Mario is
  unchanged.
- Small and big Mario also get the auto fire every 16 frames during a spin
  jump.
- The ducking and Yoshi checks still apply. With "Mario throws fireballs
  while riding Yoshi, at any power-up" (`DDAA-07A7`), small and big Mario can
  fire on Yoshi too.
- `ShootFireball` sets `ShootFireTimer`, which shows pose `$3F` on the ground
  and `$16` in the air. Those poses were not checked for small Mario, so his
  throwing pose may look wrong.
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Mario enters pipes without pressing a direction

**Codes:** `F2ED-D76F`
**Raw form:** `00F40E:1D` (orig `$3D`) (address:new-byte — the original byte is
documentation, not part of the code; SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-12 02:10:35

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00F40A` (`bank_00.asm`) starts a pipe entry. Both pipe
checks jump to it with X set to the pipe direction. `CODE_00F3C4` handles side
pipes (X = 0 or 1, tile `$13F`, Mario on the ground and facing the pipe).
`CODE_00F3E9` handles up and down pipes (X = 2 or 3, tiles `$137`/`$138`, Mario
lined up with the pipe). The routine then checks the D-pad:

```
DATA_00F3E5:
    db $02,$01,$08,$04        ; at $00F3E5 (Left, Right, Up, Down)

CODE_00F40A:
    STA.B PipeTimer           ; 85 88 at $00F40A
    LDA.B byetudlrHold        ; A5 15 at $00F40C
    AND.W DATA_00F3E5,X       ; 3D E5 F3 at $00F40E
    BEQ CODE_00F43E           ; F0 2B at $00F411
    STA.B SpriteLock
    AND.B #$01
    STA.B PlayerDirection
    ...
```

The code changes `AND.W abs,X` (`$3D`) to `ORA.W abs,X` (`$1D`). Every entry
in `DATA_00F3E5` is nonzero, so the result is never zero and the `BEQ` is never
taken. Mario goes into any pipe he is lined up with, whatever he holds.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `CODE_00F40A` at `$00F40A`. The reference ROM
has `85 88 A5 15 3D E5 F3 F0 2B` at `$00F40A` and `02 01 08 04` at `$00F3E5`.
The code decodes back to its raw form with a Game Genie encoder.

**Caveats:**

- The pipe checks themselves are unchanged. Side pipes still need Mario on the
  ground and facing the pipe. Up and down pipes still need him lined up with
  the opening.
- Walking onto the top of a down pipe takes Mario in at once, so some pipes
  can no longer be stood on or jumped across.
- When Mario comes out of a pipe onto an enterable opening, he may go straight
  back in and loop between two rooms. This was not checked.
- `PlayerDirection` comes from the Right bit of the D-pad. Mario may face right
  in a pipe where he faced left before.
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Mario enters doors in the air and without pressing Up

**Codes:** `DD3D-D407` `DD3D-D7A7`
**Raw form:** `00EC09:00` (orig `$1A`); `00EC0F:00` (orig `$14`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-12 02:10:59

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00EBDD` (`bank_00.asm`) picks out door tiles: `$20`
(door), `$1F` (small-only door), `$28`/`$27` (P-switch doors, only while
`BluePSwitchTimer` runs) and `$9C` (castle door, only in the castle
tileset). `CheckDoorEnterable` checks that Mario is lined up with the door. Then
`CODE_00EC06` checks the ground and the Up button:

```
CODE_00EC06:
    LDA.B TempPlayerAir       ; A5 8F at $00EC06
    BNE Normal_IP1            ; D0 1A at $00EC08
    LDA.B byetudlrFrame       ; A5 16 at $00EC0A
    AND.B #$08                ; 29 08 at $00EC0C
    BEQ Normal_IP1            ; F0 14 at $00EC0E
    LDA.B #!SFX_DOOROPEN
    STA.W SPCIO3
    JSR CODE_00D273
    LDA.B #$0D
    STA.B PlayerAnimation
    ...
```

Both codes set a branch displacement to `$00`. A branch of zero lands on the
next instruction, so neither check can skip the door code. Mario goes through
any door he is lined up with, in the air or on the ground.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `CODE_00EC06` at `$00EC06` and `Normal_IP1` at
`$00EC24`. The reference ROM has `A5 8F D0 1A A5 16 29 08 F0 14` at `$00EC06`.
`$00EC0A + $1A` and `$00EC10 + $14` are both `$00EC24`. The codes decode back
to their raw forms with a Game Genie encoder.

**Caveats:**

- Doors can no longer be walked or jumped past. Mario goes in as soon as he
  lines up with one.
- Small-only doors still need small Mario, and P-switch doors still need the
  P-switch.
- Either code works alone:

  | Code | Raw (original) | Effect |
  |---|---|---|
  | `DD3D-D407` | `00EC09:00` (`$1A`) | Press Up to enter a door in the air too |
  | `DD3D-D7A7` | `00EC0F:00` (`$14`) | Enter a door on the ground without pressing Up |

- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Mario does cape spins without the cape

**Codes:** `DD21-DFAD` `DDA0-AFD7`
**Raw form:** `00D067:00` (orig `$19`); `00CF44:00` (orig `$03`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-12 02:11:23

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start` `video-ready`

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00D062` (`bank_00.asm`) handles the X/Y button for the
cape and the fire flower. Only cape Mario gets to the cape spin:

```
CODE_00D062:
    LDA.B Powerup             ; A5 19 at $00D062
    CMP.B #$02                ; C9 02 at $00D064
    BNE CODE_00D081           ; D0 19 at $00D066
    BIT.B byetudlrFrame
    BVC Return00D0AD
    ...
    LDA.B #$12
    STA.W CapeSpinTimer
```

The first code sets that `BNE` displacement to `$00`, so every power-up goes
on to the spin. `CapeSpinTimer` gives the spin poses through the same code as a
spin jump, which already works for every power-up.

The spin poses code turns on the cape's hitbox only for cape Mario:

```
    LDY.B Powerup             ; A4 19 at $00CF3F
    CPY.B #$02                ; C0 02 at $00CF41
    BNE +                     ; D0 03 at $00CF43
    JSR CODE_00D044           ; 20 44 D0 at $00CF45
```

`CODE_00D044` sets `CapeInteracts` and the hitbox position next to Mario. The
second code sets the `BNE` displacement to `$00`, so the hitbox is there for
every power-up. Without it, the spin hits nothing.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `CODE_00D062` at `$00D062` and
`CODE_00D081` at `$00D081`. The reference ROM has `A5 19 C9 02 D0 19` at
`$00D062` (`$00D068 + $19 = $00D081`) and `A4 19 C0 02 D0 03 20 44 D0` at
`$00CF3F`. The codes decode back to their raw forms with a Game Genie
encoder.

**Caveats:**

- Fire Mario loses his fireballs, since `CODE_00D081` is never reached. This
  also cancels "Small and big Mario throw fireballs" (`DD26-DFDD`).
- The second code also gives small, big and fire Mario the cape hitbox in a
  spin jump, as cape Mario has.
- The ducking, Yoshi and spin jump checks still apply.
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Mario breathes out a steady stream of bubbles

**Codes:** `D5ED-0407` `D5EF-0D07`
**Raw form:** `00FD09:07` (orig `$3F`); `00FD11:07` (orig `$7F`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-12 20:24:33

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00FD08` (`bank_00.asm`) makes Mario's breath bubbles
(extended sprite `$12`). It runs on every frame that Mario is in water. It
only makes a bubble on frames where `EffFrame` AND a mask is zero:

```
CODE_00FD08:
    LDY.B #$3F                ; A0 3F at $00FD08
    LDA.B byetudlrHold
    AND.B #$83                ; B/A, left, or right held?
    BNE +
    LDY.B #$7F                ; A0 7F at $00FD10
  + TYA
    AND.B EffFrame
    ORA.B SpriteLock
    BNE Return00FD23
```

The mask is `$3F` while B/A or left/right is held, and `$7F` if not. This is
one bubble every 64 or 128 frames. The codes set both masks to `$07`, so
Mario breathes out a bubble every 8 frames.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `CODE_00FD08` at `$00FD08`. The reference ROM
has `A0 3F A5 15 29 83 D0 02 A0 7F` at `$00FD08`. The codes decode back to
their raw forms with a Game Genie encoder.

**Caveats:**

- On its own, this works only in water. With "Mario exhales bubbles on dry
  land (out-of-water bubble breathing)" (`F930-67D4` `6DBF-AF08`), the
  stream also comes out on land.
- Each bubble uses an extended-sprite slot until it pops or leaves the
  screen. A steady stream can fill the eight slots, and then fireballs,
  sparkles and other extended sprites cannot spawn.
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Hold Y or X to throw fireballs with no delay

**Code:** `F926-D70D`
**Raw form:** `00D08D:15` (orig `$16`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-25 18:45:15

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00D081` (`bank_00.asm`), the Fire Mario half of
`HandleCapeSpinAndFireball`, throws a fireball only on the frame Y or X is
first pressed:

```
CODE_00D081:
    CMP.B #$03
    BNE Return00D0AD
    LDA.B PlayerIsDucking
    ORA.W PlayerRidingYoshi
    BNE Return00D0AD
    BIT.B byetudlrFrame       ; 24 16 at $00D08C
    BVS CODE_00D0AA
```

So the player has to let go and press again for each fireball. The code
changes the operand from `byetudlrFrame` (`$16`) to `byetudlrHold`
(`$15`). Now `ShootFireball` runs on every frame Y or X is held. It
throws a new fireball as soon as one of its two slots (`$08`-`$09`) is
free, so a fireball comes out each time an old one hits something or
leaves the screen.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `CODE_00D081` at `$00D081`. The reference
ROM has `C9 03 D0 28 A5 73 0D 7A 18 D0 21 24 16 70 1A` at `$00D081`. The
code decodes back to its raw form with a Game Genie encoder.

**Caveats:**

- Y is also the run button, so Fire Mario throws fireballs the whole time
  he runs.
- Still two fireballs at a time. With "Mario gets four fireballs at once"
  (`D9E8-6D07`), the stream is thicker.
- In a spin jump, holding Y or X throws fireballs as fast as the slots
  free up, instead of one every 16 frames.
- The cape spin does not change. It still needs a new press.
- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.

## Every sound effect comes from the wrong sound list

**Codes:** `076B-0DAD` + `0D6B-07AD` (use both)
**Raw form:** `008193:43` (orig `$40`); `00819F:40` (orig `$43`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-27 19:38:39

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the ALttP code "Every sound
effect comes from the wrong sound list". The game plays a sound by
storing its ID in `SPCIO0` (`$1DF9`), `SPCIO1` (`$1DFA`) or `SPCIO3`
(`$1DFC`). Each one is its own sound list. Once per frame, `I_NMI`
(`bank_00.asm`) sends each one to its own port of the sound chip:

```
 ++ LDA.W SPCIO0          ; $00818F  AD F9 1D
    STA.W HW_APUIO0       ; $008192  8D 40 21  <- operand $40 patched
    LDA.W SPCIO1
    STA.W HW_APUIO1       ;          (port 1 is not changed)
    LDA.W SPCIO3          ; $00819B  AD FC 1D
    STA.W HW_APUIO3       ; $00819E  8D 43 21  <- operand $43 patched
```

The codes swap ports 0 and 3 (`$2140` and `$2143`). Now every port 0
sound plays the port 3 sound with the same ID, and every port 3 sound
plays the port 0 sound with that ID. Some of them (IDs from the `!SFX_`
lists in `constants.asm`):

| Sound | Port | ID | Now plays |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coin | 3 | `$01` | bonk |
| Item comes out of a block | 3 | `$02` | splat |
| Spin jump | 3 | `$04` | pipe |
| 1-up | 3 | `$05` | midway point |
| Fireball | 3 | `$06` | Yoshi's gulp |
| Block shatters | 3 | `$07` | Dry Bones collapse |
| Spring | 3 | `$08` | spin-jump kill |
| Yoshi's tongue | 3 | `$21` | rumbling starts |
| Message box | 3 | `$22` | rumbling stops |
| Enemy hurt | 3 | `$28` | firework |
| Bonk on a block | 0 | `$01` | coin |
| Kick | 0 | `$03` | vine block |
| Pipe | 0 | `$04` | spin jump |
| Midway point | 0 | `$05` | 1-up |
| Spin-jump kill | 0 | `$08` | spring |
| Cape | 0 | `$09` | kapow |
| Mushroom | 0 | `$0A` | Yoshi egg hatching |
| Stomp | 0 | `$13` | Yoshi hurt |
| Dragon coin | 0 | `$1C` | switch block |

The jump, Yoshi drums and other port 1 sounds don't change. Music
(`SPCIO2`, port 2) doesn't change.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM (`comparison_U.smc`, 512-byte copier
header) has `AD F9 1D 8D 40 21 AD FA 1D 8D 41 21 AD FC 1D 8D 43 21` once,
at `$00818F`. A script read back `$40` at `$008193` and `$43` at
`$00819F`. The other writes to `HW_APUIO0` and `HW_APUIO3` are in the
sound upload code (`UploadDataToSPC`, `StartMusicUpload`), not in this
part of the NMI. Both codes decode back to their raw forms with
`snes_gg_encode.py`. The same bytes are at `$00818F` in `SMW_SS.smc`,
`SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc`. In `SMW_J.smc` they are at `$008180`, so
J needs `0766-0FDD` + `0D6B-0DDD` (`008184:43`, `008190:40`) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- Use both codes. With only one, both stores go to the same port and
  the later one wins, even when it writes `$00`. Half the sounds would
  never play.
- The sound program treats some port 0 IDs as commands, so these change
  too:
  - Pause (`$11`) and unpause (`$12`) now play the drumroll start and end
    sounds. The music no longer goes quiet while paused.
  - The bonus-star drumroll after a goal (port 3 `$11`, `$12`) now acts
    as pause and unpause for the music.
  - At 99 seconds, the "hurry up" command (`$FF`) goes to port 3. The
    music doesn't speed up. Port 3 has no range check, so `$FF` reads a
    pointer from past the end of its table and may play noise or stop
    the sound.
- The port 0 list has 42 sounds and port 3 has 52. Port 3 IDs `$2B`-`$34`
  (Bowser's flames in the final fight and the last fireworks) read
  pointers from past the end of the port 0 table. They may play noise or
  stop the sound.
- Yoshi's tongue starts the rumbling sound. It may go on until a message
  box plays "rumbling stops".

## Hold Y or X to cape spin nonstop

**Code:** `F921-D40D`
**Raw form:** `00D069:15` (orig `$16`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-27 19:52:00

**Mechanism:** This is the cape version of "Hold Y or X to throw fireballs
with no delay". `HandleCapeSpinAndFireball` (`bank_00.asm`) starts a cape
spin only on the frame Y or X is first pressed:

```
HandleCapeSpinAndFireball:
    LDA.B Powerup
    CMP.B #$02
    BNE CODE_00D081
    BIT.B byetudlrFrame       ; 24 16 at $00D068
    BVC Return00D0AD
    LDA.B PlayerIsDucking
    ORA.W PlayerRidingYoshi
    ORA.W SpinJumpFlag
    BNE Return00D0AD
    LDA.B #$12
    STA.W CapeSpinTimer
```

So the player has to let go and press again for each spin. The code
changes the operand from `byetudlrFrame` (`$16`) to `byetudlrHold`
(`$15`). Now `CapeSpinTimer` is set back to `$12` on every frame Y or X
is held, so it never runs out. The spin pose comes from `EffFrame`, not
from the timer (the `SpinJumpFlag` / `CapeSpinTimer` check near
`lbl14A2Not0`), so Mario keeps turning instead of freezing on one
frame. When the button is let go, the timer counts down in the timer
loop at `CODE_00C508` and the last spin ends as usual.

**Evidence:** `SMW_U.sym` puts `HandleCapeSpinAndFireball` at `$00D062`.
The reference ROM has `A5 19 C9 02 D0 19 24 16 50 41 A5 73 0D 7A 18 0D
0D 14 D0 37 A9 12 8D A6` at `$00D062`. The code decodes back to its raw
form with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc` has the same bytes at the
same address. In `SMW_J.smc`, `SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` the routine
is at `$00D002`, so those need `F92D-D40D` (`00D009:15`) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.
- Y is also the run button, so cape Mario spins the whole time he runs.
  Holding an item also holds Y, so he spins while he carries it. What
  the spin does to the carried item was not checked.
- The spin sound plays once per press, not on every frame. The sound
  program starts a port 3 sound only when the value on the port
  changes, and the code writes `!SFX_SPIN` every frame.
- Still no spin while ducking, on Yoshi or in a spin jump.
- With "Mario does cape spins without the cape" (`DD21-DFAD` +
  `DDA0-AFD7`), small, big and fire Mario spin nonstop too.

## Hold Y to cape spin or throw fireballs nonstop

**Code:** `C468-64DF`
**Raw form:** `0086B8:A2` (orig `$A8`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-27 20:11:05

**Mechanism:** This does what "Hold Y or X to throw fireballs with no
delay" and "Hold Y or X to cape spin nonstop" do, in one code. Those two
codes change two separate `BIT.B byetudlrFrame` instructions in
`HandleCapeSpinAndFireball`, so one Game Genie code can't change both.
This code changes the controller routine that builds `byetudlrFrame`
instead (`bank_00.asm`, just before `InitM7BossOAM`):

```
    LDA.W axlr0000P1Frame,X   ; BD A8 0D at $0086B7  <- $A8 -> $A2
    AND.B #!ButX
    ORA.W byetudlrP1Frame,X
    STA.B byetudlrFrame
```

The game copies an X press into the Y bit (`$40`) of `byetudlrFrame`,
so X does what Y does. The code changes `axlr0000P1Frame` (`$0DA8`) to
`byetudlrP1Hold` (`$0DA2`). In `byetudlrP1Hold`, bit `$40` is Y, so now
the Y bit of `byetudlrFrame` is set on every frame Y is held. To the
game, holding Y is a new Y press on every frame. Cape Mario starts a new
cape spin on every frame, and Fire Mario throws a fireball as soon as
one of the two slots is free.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `BD A8 0D 29 40 1D A6 0D 85 16` once,
at `$0086B7`. A script read back `$A8` at `$0086B8`. `SMW_U.sym` puts
`byetudlrP1Hold` at `$0DA2` and `axlr0000P1Frame` at `$0DA8`. The code
decodes back to its raw form with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`,
`SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` have the same bytes at the same address.
In `SMW_J.smc` the byte is at `$00864D`, so J needs `C460-670F`
(`00864D:A2`) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.
- An X press no longer counts as a Y press, so X can't spin the cape,
  throw fireballs or use Yoshi's tongue. X still runs and carries items,
  since those read `byetudlrHold`.
- Y is also the run button, so the cape spin and the fireballs go on the
  whole time Mario runs.
- Other code that reads a Y press from `byetudlrFrame` also repeats
  while Y is held:
  - Yoshi sticks his tongue out over and over (`CODE_01F1DF`).
  - Mario picks up a grab block as soon as he touches it
    (`CODE_00F267`).
  - On the file-delete and player-select screens, Y goes back to file
    select. On the map, Y enters the level, which a press already does.
- With "Mario does cape spins without the cape" (`DD21-DFAD` +
  `DDA0-AFD7`), every form spins nonstop and Fire Mario no longer throws
  fireballs.

## Hold B to jump again every time Mario lands

**Code:** `F92F-640F`
**Raw form:** `00D619:15` (orig `$16`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-27 20:07:09

**Mechanism:** `CODE_00D5F2` (`bank_00.asm`) starts a jump from the ground
only on the frame B or A is first pressed:

```
    LDA.B byetudlrFrame       ; A5 16 at $00D618
    ORA.B axlr0000Frame
    BMI StartPlayerJump
```

So the player has to let go and press again for each jump. The code
changes the operand from `byetudlrFrame` (`$16`) to `byetudlrHold`
(`$15`). Now, while B is held, Mario jumps again on the first frame he
is back on the ground. B is still held during the jump, so every jump
is a full-height jump.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `A5 16 05 18 30` once, at `$00D618`.
A script read back `$16` at `$00D619`. The code decodes back to its raw
form with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc` has the same bytes at the
same address. In `SMW_J.smc`, `SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` the byte is
at `$00D5B9`, so those need `F928-040F` (`00D5B9:15`) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.
- `byetudlrHold` also has A in bit 7, so holding A bunny-hops too. But
  `StartPlayerJump` picks the spin jump only on a new A press
  (`axlr0000Frame`), so after the first spin jump, the hops are normal
  jumps. With "Hold A to spin jump nonstop" (`C06A-6D6F`), A gives spin
  jumps every time.
- Only the jump from the ground changes. Swimming and jumping off vines
  and nets still need a new press.

## Hold A to spin jump nonstop

**Code:** `C06A-6D6F`
**Raw form:** `0086C2:A4` (orig `$A8`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-27 20:07:09

**Mechanism:** The controller routine (`bank_00.asm`, just before
`InitM7BossOAM`) sets up `axlr0000Frame`, the "pressed this frame" byte
for A, X, L and R:

```
    LDA.W axlr0000P1Frame,X   ; BD A8 0D at $0086C1  <- $A8 -> $A4
    STA.B axlr0000Frame
```

The code changes `axlr0000P1Frame` (`$0DA8`) to `axlr0000P1Hold`
(`$0DA4`). Now every button in `axlr0000Frame` counts as pressed on
every frame it is held. In `CODE_00D5F2`, the ground jump starts when
`byetudlrFrame` or `axlr0000Frame` has bit 7 set, and `StartPlayerJump`
makes it a spin jump when `axlr0000Frame` has bit 7 (A) set. So while A
is held, Mario spin jumps again on the first frame he is back on the
ground.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `BD A8 0D 85 18` right after
`BD A8 0D 29 40 1D A6 0D 85 16`, at `$0086C1`. A script read back `$A8`
at `$0086C2`. The code decodes back to its raw form with
`snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`, `SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` have
the same bytes at the same address. In `SMW_J.smc` the byte is at
`$008657`, so J needs `C069-6FAF` (`008657:A4`) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested in play. The effect comes from the disassembly.
- Other code that reads an A press also repeats while A is held:
  - Mario swims nonstop (`CODE_00D9EB`).
  - Holding A jumps off Yoshi at once (`BIT.B axlr0000Frame` before
    `DismountYoshi`).
  - Message boxes close as soon as they open (`CODE_05B16E`).
  - On the title screen and file menus, holding A selects over and
    over. Let go of A there, since it could pick an erase option.
- X, L and R also count as pressed while held. Holding X also closes
  message boxes at once and works the menus and the map. Camera
  scrolling with L and R reads `axlr0000Hold`, so it doesn't change.
- Don't use with "Free-roaming debug mode (L+A)" (`EDA6-DFD7`). Its
  toggle in `ResetAni` needs `axlr0000Frame` to be exactly `$80`. While
  L is held, the byte is now `$A0`, so the debug mode never turns on.
- With "Hold B to jump again every time Mario lands" (`F92F-640F`), B
  gives normal jumps and A gives spin jumps.

## Every sound effect is the one after it in its sound list

**Codes:** `6764-6476` + `6064-6756` + `F869-AFE6` + `FA69-A776` (use all
four)
**Raw form:** `0E8228:83` (orig `$81`); `0E822D:84` (orig `$82`);
`0E8357:1B` (orig `$19`); `0E835C:1C` (orig `$1A`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-29 00:47:09

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the FF2 code "Every sound
effect is the one after it in the sound effect list". When a port 0
(`SPCIO0`) or port 3 (`SPCIO3`) sound starts, the sound program
(`bank_0E.asm`) reads its pointer from the list for that port, 2 bytes
per ID:

```
APU_071F:
    MOV.B A,SPCOutBuffer
    ASL A
    MOV Y,A
    MOV.W A,SFXPtrs1DF9-2+Y
    MOV.B SFX1DF9PhrasePtr,A
    MOV.W A,SFXPtrs1DF9-1+Y
    MOV.B SFX1DF9PhrasePtr+1,A
```

The port 3 code just before `APU_085E` is the same, with
`SFXPtrs1DFC`. The codes add 2 to the low byte of all four addresses,
so ID `n` plays the sound of ID `n+1` from the same list. The first two
codes are port 0 and the last two are port 3. Some of them (IDs from
the `!SFX_` lists in `constants.asm`):

| Sound | Port | ID | Now plays |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coin | 3 | `$01` | item comes out of a block |
| Spin jump | 3 | `$04` | 1-up |
| 1-up | 3 | `$05` | fireball |
| Spring | 3 | `$08` | kapow |
| Message box | 3 | `$22` | beep |
| Enemy hurt | 3 | `$28` | correct |
| Bonk on a block | 0 | `$01` | splat |
| Kick | 0 | `$03` | pipe |
| Cape | 0 | `$09` | mushroom |
| Mushroom | 0 | `$0A` | switch |
| Stomp | 0 | `$13`-`$18` | the next stomp in the combo |

The jump and other port 1 sounds don't change, and music doesn't
change.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM (`comparison_U.smc`) has
`F6 81 56 C4 18 F6 82 56` at `$0E8227` (`SFXPtrs1DF9` = `$5683`) and
`F6 19 56 C4 1A F6 1A 56` at `$0E8356` (`SFXPtrs1DFC` = `$561B`), each
once. Adding 2 to these low bytes doesn't carry. The sound program is
in the ROM and is uploaded at power-on (`SPC700Engine`). The codes
decode back to their raw forms with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`,
`SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` have the same bytes at the same
addresses. In `SMW_J.smc` they are 24 bytes later, so J needs
`6760-6D76` + `6060-6F56` + `F861-A7E6` + `FA65-AF76` (`0E8240:83`,
`0E8245:84`, `0E836F:1B`, `0E8374:1C`) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- The pause and unpause commands (port 0 `$11`, `$12`) and the "hurry
  up" command (`$FF`) are checked by ID before the list is read, so they
  still work.
- The last port 0 sound (`$2A`, Peach calling for help) reads past the
  end of its list and may play noise or stop the sound. The last port 3
  sound (`$34`) reads the first port 0 pointer, so it plays the bonk.
- The first two codes alone change only port 0, and the last two alone
  change only port 3.

## Every song is the one after it in its music bank

**Codes:** `1D61-6F8B` + `1F61-64EB` (use both)
**Raw form:** `0E8666:60` (orig `$5E`); `0E866B:61` (orig `$5F`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-29 00:47:09

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the FF2 code "Every song is
the one after it in the song list". When a song starts, the sound
program reads its pointer from `MusicData` (ARAM `$1360`), 2 bytes per
song:

```
 ++ MOV.B SPCOutBuffer+2,A
    MOV.B ARam_0C,#$02
    ASL A
    MOV Y,A
    MOV.W A,MusicData-2+Y
    MOV.B BlockPtr,A
    MOV.W A,MusicData-1+Y
    MOV.B BlockPtr+1,A
```

The codes add 2 to the low bytes of both addresses, so song `n` plays
song `n+1` of the music bank that is loaded. The level bank and the
overworld bank each upload their own list to `MusicData`. Some of them
(IDs from the `!BGM_` lists in `constants.asm`):

| Song | Bank | ID | Now plays |
|---|---|---|---|
| Athletic | level | `$01` | overworld-style level |
| Overworld-style level | level | `$02` | underwater |
| Underground | level | `$06` | ghost house |
| Castle | level | `$08` | death |
| Death | level | `$09` | game over |
| Level clear | level | `$0C` | star power |
| Star power | level | `$0D` | P-switch |
| Title screen | overworld | `$01` | Donut Plains |
| Yoshi's Island | overworld | `$03` | Vanilla Dome |

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `F6 5E 13 C4 40 F6 5F 13` once, at
`$0E8665` (`MusicData` = `$1360`). Adding 2 to these low bytes doesn't
carry. The level bank (`MusicBank2`) lists 29 songs and the overworld
bank (`MusicBank1`) 9. The codes decode back to their raw forms with
`snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`, `SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` have
the same bytes at the same addresses. In `SMW_J.smc` they are at
`$0E867E` and `$0E8683`, so J needs `1D65-678B` + `1F66-6DEB` instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- The last song of each bank reads past the end of the list: song `$1D`
  of the level bank (the second Bowser interlude) and song `$09` of the
  overworld bank (Special World, also used for the staff credits). They
  may play noise or stop the sound.
- Before the list is read, the sound program checks a few song IDs to
  reset the tempo (`$09`-`$0C`, `$0F`, `$10`, `$16`). These checks still
  use the old ID.
- The credits bank (`MusicBank3`) shifts too.

## Every song plays with the next instrument

**Code:** `0869-DF5C`
**Raw form:** `0E8855:4B` (orig `$46`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-29 00:47:09

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start`

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the FF2 code "Every song
plays with the instruments of the next song". Voice command `$DA` sets a
voice's instrument. The sound program reads the instrument from a table
at ARAM `$5F46`, 5 bytes each (sample, ADSR 1 and 2, gain, pitch
multiplier):

```
APU_0D4B:
    MOV.B VoInstrument+1+X,A
    DEC A
    MOV Y,#$05
    MOV.B ARam_14,#$46
    MOV.B ARam_15,#$5F

APU_0D56:
    MUL YA                                    ; set sample A in bank at $14/15 width Y;
    ADDW.B YA,ARam_14
```

The code changes the `#$46` to `#$4B`, so the table starts 5 bytes
later. Every instrument `n` in a song plays instrument `n+1`, with that
instrument's sample, envelope and pitch multiplier. The notes don't
change.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `8F 46 14 8F 5F 15` once, at
`$0E8854`. The table has 19 instruments, from `$5F46` up to the
percussion table at `$5FA5` (`APU_0D56` with width 6). The code decodes
back to its raw form with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`,
`SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` have the same byte at the same address. In
`SMW_J.smc` it is at `$0E886D`, so J needs `0861-D75C` instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- Each instrument has its own pitch multiplier, so the new instrument
  can play in a different key or octave from the old one.
- The last instrument (`$12`) reads the first 5 bytes of the percussion
  table, which are laid out differently. It may play a wrong sample.
- Percussion notes (`$D0` and up) use their own table and don't
  change. Sound effects set their instruments from `SFXDSPSettings`
  and don't change either.

## Music and sound effects play an octave higher

**Code:** `D962-0FE8`
**Raw form:** `0E8DD7:05` (orig `$06`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Optional, instead, an octave lower:** `D562-0FE8` (`0E8DD7:07`)
**Optional, instead, two octaves lower:** `D662-0FE8` (`0E8DD7:08`)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-29 00:47:09

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the FF2 code "Music and sound
effects play half an octave higher". `GetPitch` (`bank_0E.asm`) turns a
note number into a pitch. It splits the note into an octave (`X`) and
one of 12 values from `PitchTable`, then halves the value once for each
octave below 6:

```
GetPitch:
    MOV Y,#$00                                ; get pitch from note number in A (with octave correction) to YA;to YA
    ASL A
    MOV X,#$18
    DIV YA,X
    MOV X,A
    MOV.W A,PitchTable+1+Y
    MOV.B PitchValue,A
    MOV.W A,PitchTable+Y
    BRA +
  - LSR.B PitchValue
    ROR A
    INC X
  + CMP X,#$06
    BNE -
```

The code changes the `#$06` to `#$05`, so every note is halved one time
less and plays an octave higher. The optional codes use `#$07` (one more
halving, an octave lower) or `#$08` (two octaves lower). Songs and
sound effects both get their pitch from `GetPitch`, so both change. No
byte changes only one of them.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `C8 06 D0 F8` once, at `$0E8DD6`,
right after the `DIV YA,X` and the `PitchTable` reads. The code decodes
back to its raw form with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`,
`SMW_E0.smc` and `SMW_E1.smc` have the same byte at the same address. In
`SMW_J.smc` it is at `$0E8DEF`, so J needs `D963-07E8` (higher) or
`D563-07E8` (lower) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- Note numbers `$80`-`$C5` give octaves 0-5. The loop counts up from
  the octave until it reaches the new number. With `#$05`, a note in
  octave 6 or above (only possible with the global transpose, voice
  command `$E4`) never matches until `X` wraps around. Its pitch is halved
  255 times and the note is silent.
- Going up, high notes with a large instrument pitch multiplier can pass
  the DSP's largest pitch and play a wrong note.

## Music and sound effects play with 5 of the 12 notes out of place

**Codes:** `F563-0D78` + `FB63-0F88` + `FF63-0488` + `F463-0788` +
`F56E-0F78` (use all 5)
**Raw form:** `0E8DE0:17` (orig `$11`); `0E8DE6:19` (orig `$15`);
`0E8DEA:11` (orig `$17`); `0E8DEE:12` (orig `$1A`); `0E8DF4:17` (orig
`$1F`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-29 01:05:07

Tags: `demo-ready` `play-start`

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the FF2 code with the same
name. `GetPitch` (`bank_0E.asm`) gets the pitch of each note from
`PitchTable`, 12 values from C to B, and halves it for the octave (see
"Music and sound effects play an octave higher"):

```
PitchTable:
    dw $10BE, $11BD, $12CB, $13E9, $1518, $1659
    dw $17AD, $1916, $1A94, $1C28, $1DD5, $1F9B
```

The codes change the high byte of 5 of the values, so those notes play
at the wrong pitch in every octave and the other 7 stay put. They move
by the same amounts as in the FF2 code:

| Note | Was | Now | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| C# | `$11BD` | `$17BD` | 5 semitones up |
| E | `$1518` | `$1918` | 3 semitones up |
| F# | `$17AD` | `$11AD` | 5 semitones down |
| G# | `$1A94` | `$1294` | 6 semitones down |
| B | `$1F9B` | `$179B` | 5 semitones down |

No new value is above `$1F9B`, so this adds no notes past the DSP's
largest pitch.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM (`comparison_U.smc`) has `BE 10 BD 11
CB 12 E9 13 18 15 59 16 AD 17 16 19 94 1A 28 1C D5 1D 9B 1F` once, at
`$0E8DDD`, right after the octave loop of `GetPitch`. A script read
back the orig byte at each code's address. The codes decode back to
their raw forms with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`, `SMW_E0.smc`
and `SMW_E1.smc` have the same bytes at the same addresses. In
`SMW_J.smc` the table is at `$0E8DF5`, so J needs `F56E-0478` +
`FB6E-0788` + `FF6D-6D88` + `F46D-6F88` + `F56D-6778` instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- Sound effects use the same table, so some of them change pitch too.
- Between two notes (pitch slides, vibrato and fine tuning), the sound
  program adds a part of the gap to the next value. Next to a changed
  value the gap can be negative, so those in-between pitches can jump.

## Music and sound effects play one semitone higher

**Codes:** `6663-D486` + `666F-DD78` + `DF63-D4E6` + `DF6F-DD58` (use
all four)
**Raw form:** `0E80EA:88` (orig `$84`); `0E8C10:88` (orig `$84`);
`0E80EB:01` (orig `$43`); `0E8C11:01` (orig `$43`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Optional, instead, one semitone lower:** `6663-D486` + `666F-DD78` + `EE63-D4E6` + `EE6F-DD58`
(`0E80EB:FF`, `0E8C11:FF`)
**Recorded:** 2026-10-29 01:05:07

**Mechanism:** This is the SMW version of the FF2 code with the same
name. FF2 changes a constant that is subtracted from every note. SMW
has no such constant, but it adds the global transpose (`MasterTranspose`,
`$43`, set by voice command `$E4`) to every note:

```
APU_05E3:
    AND A,#$7F
    CLRC
    ADC.B A,MasterTranspose                   ; add global transpose
    MOV.W ARam_02B0+1+X,A
```

The pitch slide command (`$DD`) adds it to the note it slides to, a bit
before `APU_1111`:

```
    CALL NextVCmd
    CLRC
    ADC.B A,MasterTranspose
    CALL APU_0F5D
```

The first two codes change both `ADC.B A,MasterTranspose` (`84 43`) to
`ADC A,#imm` (`88`), and the last two set the number to add to `$01`.
Every note is now one semitone higher. The optional codes add `$FF`,
which is one semitone lower. Songs and sound effects both send their
notes through `HandleVCmd`, so both change.

**Evidence:** The reference ROM has `28 7F 60 84 43 D5` once, at
`$0E80E7`, and `60 84 43 3F 5D 0F` once, at `$0E8C0F`. These are the
only two reads of `MasterTranspose` in `bank_0E.asm`. A script read
back the orig byte at each code's address. The codes decode back to
their raw forms with `snes_gg_encode.py`. `SMW_SS.smc`, `SMW_E0.smc`
and `SMW_E1.smc` have the same bytes at the same addresses. In
`SMW_J.smc` they are 24 bytes later, so J needs `666D-0D86` +
`6664-D478` + `DF6D-0DE6` + `DF64-D458` (lower: `EE6D-0DE6` +
`EE64-D458` for the last two) instead.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- Use all four codes. Without the second and fourth, pitch slides end at
  the old pitch.
- The global transpose is replaced, not added to. A song that sets a
  transpose with `$E4` plays at the cheat's shift instead.
- Going down, the lowest note (C of octave 0, `$80`) wraps around to a
  very high note number, and is silent.
- A one-semitone shift is small. Many players won't notice it unless
  they know the songs well.

**Caveats:**

- Not tested.
- The caveats of the one-semitone entry apply. Going down, the 4 lowest
  notes are silent.
- Going up, the highest notes can pass the DSP's largest pitch and play
  a wrong note.
- These write the same 4 bytes as the other semitone cheats. Use only
  one.

## Auto-scroll levels scroll freely: the screen follows Mario

**Codes:** `D068-0729` + `C287-0FB5` + `9386-D495` + `C2AD-DF90` +
`608B-D725` (use all five)
**Optional, for Donut Plains 2:** `B588-D4B5`
**Raw form:** `0585BF:04` (orig `$03`); `05BD36:AD` (orig `$9C`);
`05BC89:5E` (orig `$4D`); `05C005:AD` (orig `$9C`); `05BC9F:84` (orig
`$87`); optional `05BCBA:97` (orig `$98`)
(address:new-byte — the original byte is documentation, not part of the code;
SNES Game Genie has no compare byte)
**Recorded:** 2026-11-01 01:44:01

**Mechanism:** A forced-scroll level places a scroll sprite at its start.
The sprite loader in `bank_02.asm` stores `sprite number - $E7` in
`Layer1ScrollCmd` and calls `CODE_05BCD6`, which runs the command's setup
routine from the table in `CODE_05BCE9`. After that, `ProcScreenScrollCmds`
runs the command's per-frame routine every frame, from the table in
`CODE_05BC76` (and, for `Layer2ScrollCmd`, the table in `CODE_05BCA5`). Two
commands make the screen move by itself:

- **01** (sprite `$E8`, `%S_AutoScroll` types `dp2`, `bb1`, `coinheaven`):
  setup `InitSpecialAutoScrollL1`, per-frame `ProcSpecAutoScrollL1`.
- **0C** (sprite `$F3`, types `slow` and `fast`): setup `InitAutoScroll`,
  per-frame `ProcAutoScroll`.

The camera follows Mario sideways only when `HorizLayer1Setting` is not
zero (`UpdateScreenPosition` skips that code otherwise). The flag also
makes the left edge of the screen push Mario (`CODE_00E9C8`) and turns off
the L/R screen scroll (`CODE_00CDDD`). `CODE_05D796` sets it to 1 from the
level header, and two things clear it in these levels:

- `CODE_0584E3` clears it while the level data loads, when the header's
  scroll setting is 3 (`CMP.B #$03 / BNE + / STZ.W HorizLayer1Setting /
  LDA.B #$00 / + STA.W VertLayer1Setting`). Setting 3 is used only by four
  of the auto-scroll levels (`009_DP2main`, `00C_BB1main`, `01F_FFroom1`,
  `1FC_C1room2`) and the unused `betaclouds`.
- Both scroll setups begin with `STZ.W HorizLayer1Setting`.

The codes:

- Code 1 changes the `CMP.B #$03` operand to `$04`. The scroll setting is
  2 bits, so it never matches. The flag stays 1, and `VertLayer1Setting`
  gets 3. `CODE_00F7F4` treats any value other than 0 and 1 like setting
  2, so the screen scrolls up and down when Mario flies, climbs and so on.
- Codes 2 and 4 change both setups' `STZ.W HorizLayer1Setting` (`9C 11 14`)
  to `LDA.W HorizLayer1Setting` (`AD 11 14`). The next instruction is an
  `LDA`, so the loaded value is not used.
- Code 3 points per-frame entry 01 (`$05BC89`, normally `ProcSpecAutoScrollL1`
  at `$05C04D`) at `$05C05E`, the `RTS` that ends the routine's "timer is 0"
  path.
- Code 5 points per-frame entry 0C (`$05BC9F`, normally `ProcAutoScroll` at
  `$05C787`) at `CODE_05C784` (`JMP CODE_05C32B`, which is `SEP #$20 / RTS`).
- The optional code is for `009_DP2main`. Its scroll bits make
  `InitSpecialAutoScrollL1` also set `Layer2ScrollCmd` to 01 (from
  `DATA_05C9D1`), and the Layer 2 per-frame routine `ProcSpecAutoScrollL2`
  copies `NextLayer2XPos` into `NextLayer1XPos` every frame. So without
  this code, Layer 2 still drags the screen in that level. It points Layer
  2 per-frame entry 01 (`$05BCBA`, normally `ProcSpecAutoScrollL2` at
  `$05C198`) at `$05C197`, the `RTS` just before it. Only this setup sets
  `Layer2ScrollCmd` to 01.

The setup routines still run, so `Layer1ScrollCmd` keeps its value. The
per-frame routines are just empty.

**Where you see it:** `009_DP2main`, `00C_BB1main`, `0C8_yoshiwingsdark`
(command 01), and `01F_FFroom1`, `1D4_FDroom1`, `1FC_C1room2`,
`1C8_yoshiwingsbright` (command 0C). Names are from `lvl/spr/`.

**Evidence:** Bytes read from `comparison_U.smc` (minus its 512-byte copier
header): `$0585B8` reads `29 30 4A 4A 4A 4A C9 03 D0 05 9C 11 14 A9 00 8D 12
14`, so the `CMP` operand is at `$0585BF`. `CODE_05BC76` reads `... 22 DF 86
00 4D C0 4D C0 ...`, so per-frame entry 01 at `$05BC89` is `4D C0`, and entry
0C at `$05BC9F` is `87 C7`. `CODE_05BCA5` reads `... 22 DF 86 00 4D C0 98 C1
...`, so Layer 2 entry 01 at `$05BCBA` is `98 C1`. `$05BD36` and `$05C005`
both read `9C 11 14`. `$05C05E` is `60`, `$05C784` is `4C 2B C3`, `$05C32B`
is `E2 20 60`, `$05C195` is `E2 20 60`. Routine addresses are from
`SMW_U.sym`. The codes decode back to their raw forms with
`snes_gg_encode.py`. The header scroll settings are from the `%L_Header`
lines in `lvl/obj/`.

**Revisions:** U, E0 and SS have the same bytes at all six addresses and at
the targets. E1 has the same bytes at the bank 05 `$BC76`-`$C800` addresses,
but the `CMP` operand is at `$0585E4`, so E1's code 1 is `D063-0FF9`. In
`SMW_J.smc` the `CMP` operand is at the same `$0585BF`, but the bank 05
`$BC76`-`$C800` code is `$100` bytes earlier, so J's codes 2-5 and the
optional code are `C287-DFB5` + `9386-A491` + `C28D-AF95` + `608B-A721` +
`B588-A4B1` (`05BC36:AD`, `05BB89:5E`, `05BF05:AD`, `05BB9F:84`,
`05BBBA:97`; bytes and targets checked in `SMW_J.smc`).

**Caveats:**

- Tested on 2026-11-01 (all six codes, U ROM, in Mesen2): the screen
  follows Mario.
- Turn the codes on before you enter the level. The setup runs once, when
  the scroll sprite loads at the start of the level, and code 1 is read
  while the level loads.
- The levels were built for a screen that moves at a set speed, so some
  parts may play differently when you can stop or go back.
- `009_DP2main`: Layer 2 is a second solid layer there (`009_DP2main_l2`).
  With the optional code, it moves the way the level header's Layer 2
  scroll setting says, not on the scroll path.
- The `coinheaven` level also sets `Layer2ScrollCmd` to 09 (the fast Layer 2
  background scroll). That is not changed, so its background still moves.
- These codes conflict with "The auto-scroll sprite runs one of the unused
  scroll commands 04, 05 or 0A" and "The auto-scroll sprite runs an unused
  scroll: the screen moves up and down 48 pixels and shakes at each end".
  They write `$05BC89` too.
